Imo monarch’s murder: 5 suspects arrested, gang kingpin killed in shootout
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Force headquarters disclosed on Saturday that Police operatives have recorded a breakthrough in the ongoing investigation into the murder of HRH Eze Paulinus Ekwueme, Ochia I of Ochia Kingdom, and five others in Ohaji/Egbema, Imo State. Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Aniete Iniedu, made the disclosure, noting that two other suspects were killed during exchange of fire between the gang and policemen. He said, “Following actionable intelligence, operatives of the Special Tactics Squad, Force Intelligence Department (STS-FID), conducted a series of operations between 2nd and 6th August, 2026, targeting members of the criminal syndicate allegedly linked to the incident. “The operations culminated in the early hours of 6th August, 2026, when operatives located the hideout of a suspected gang kingpin, identified as Ojiogu Elumah Martin, alias ‘Acid’, in Ohaji/Egbema. “The suspect engaged the operatives in a gun duel and sustained injuries during the encounter, which subsequently led to his death. One AK-47 rifle, three magazines and 56 rounds of 7.62mm live ammunition were recovered from the scene. “The suspect was identified as an alleged leader of the criminal syndicate linked to the attack of 10th April, 2026, in which the monarch and five others were killed along the Asa/Awara Road, Ohaji/Egbema, while returning to Owerri. “Four suspects had earlier been arrested in connection with the incident, while two others reportedly died during previous encounters with the Police. “Following the latest operation, efforts have been intensified to apprehend other fleeing members of the syndicate, establish the full extent of their involvement and recover further operational intelligence and exhibits. “The Nigeria Police Force remains committed to ensuring that all persons found to be connected with the crime are brought to justice and that every effort is made to bring the investigation to a logical conclusion.” The post Imo monarch’s murder: 5 suspects arrested, gang kingpin killed in shootout appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: History Made, Future Beckons: How Oloyede’s stewardship redefined JAMB, restored public trust
items.description: By Ishola Balogun After ten eventful years at the helm of the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB), Professor Is-haq Olanrewaju Oloyede on Friday formally handed over the leadership of Nigeria’s foremost admissions agency to Professor Segun Aina, bringing to a close a tenure widely associated with sweeping institutional reforms, technological innovation, financial transparency and renewed public confidence in the nation’s tertiary admissions process. Read Also: 25 children from Kebbi, Kwara, Niger died in terrorists’ captivity — Lawmaker Speaking at the handover ceremony held at JAMB’s National Headquarters in Bwari, Abuja, Prof. Oloyede described the occasion as both a moment of gratitude and reflection, declaring that whatever achievements were recorded during his stewardship were products of divine grace and collective effort rather than personal accomplishment. “It is with a profound sense of gratitude to the Almighty Allah and immense appreciation to all people of goodwill that I address this distinguished audience today,” he said. “I return all glory to Almighty Allah, whose boundless mercy, wisdom and grace sustained me throughout these remarkable ten years. Through periods of daunting challenges, difficult policy decisions and far-reaching institutional reforms, His guidance remained my greatest source of strength. Whatever accomplishments have been recorded during this period are not mine alone; they are manifestations of His infinite favour and blessings.” The outgoing Registrar recalled that when he assumed office on August 9, 2016, he deliberately chose the theme, “Let’s Do It Together,” believing that no institution could succeed without collaboration. “I had no illusion right from the outset that I would depend on God’s guidance and people’s support,” he said. “Doing it together means that many colours make a rainbow and many flowers make a garden.” A decade built on five pillars Reflecting on his stewardship, Prof. Oloyede said his administration was anchored on five cardinal principles—staff welfare, discipline, technology, transparency and networking—which became the foundation of JAMB’s transformation. “When I took over the mandate of leadership at JAMB, I outlined five cardinal points that my administration would be anchored on… In these five, though perfection belongs to the Almighty Allah, I can confidently say we tried our best.” Welfare before productivity He explained that his administration invested heavily in staff welfare, arguing that no institution could outperform the people who run it. Among the initiatives introduced were timely promotions, improved work environments, rehabilitation and construction of offices nationwide, over N8 billion contributed to staff retirement savings, retirement benefits ranging between N3 million and N10 million, the introduction of a 13th-month salary, examination duty allowances increased from 10 to 20 per cent, free daily meals, transport support for key operational staff and medical interventions, including N12 million approved for the treatment of a staff member at the National Hospital. Exceptional staff were rewarded with cash prizes and awards, while one zonal office and a Professional Test Centre complex were named after a deserving employee. “We stood by our decision because without dedicated and motivated staff, we won’t achieve the JAMB that Nigeria deserves,” he declared. Beyond staff welfare, he said candidates also benefited from reforms, including a 30 per cent reduction in the UTME application cost and comprehensive support for candidates with special needs through sponsorship, accommodation, feeding and refund of application fees. The Board also extended institutional support through the National Tertiary Admissions Performance Merit (NATAPM) Award, disbursing approximately ¦ 750 million annually to tertiary institutions. Discipline without compromise While investing in welfare, Oloyede maintained that discipline remained non-negotiable. “It is said that the first law in heaven is discipline and indiscipline is the mother of all evils.” According to him, more than ten staff members faced prosecution over allegations of misconduct during his tenure. He recalled the widely publicised case involving the infamous claim that a snake swallowed ¦ 36 million, describing it as one of the disciplinary measures undertaken to restore accountability. “The sensationalised case of a snake gulping N36 million that the media feasted on was just one of the measures taken to entrench discipline,” he said, recalling that even the EFCC had remarked at the time that “an eagle shows no mercy for money-swallowing snakes.” He added that the insistence on discipline accounted for JAMB’s consistent remittance of billions of naira in operational surpluses to the Federal Government. Technology as the engine of reform Perhaps the defining feature of his administration, Oloyede noted, was JAMB’s aggressive deployment of technology. He listed the expansion of Computer-Based Testing (CBT), development of the Central Admissions Processing System (CAPS), biometric identity verification, CCTV surveillance, digital PINs and payment platforms, Remote Authoring and Moderation System (RAMS), digital institutional reforms and the Bring-Your-Device initiative as milestones achieved during the decade. “At the heart of our operational blueprint is technology and we owe many of our far-reaching reforms to innovative technologies,” he said. Reflecting on recent technical challenges experienced during the UTME, Oloyede admitted that no technology is infallible. “What happened last year which made me emotional was proof that technology has its limits, just like everything human, and eternal vigilance is the price of liberty.” Transparency restores confidence On transparency, the outgoing Registrar said his administration deliberately opened JAMB’s operations to public scrutiny. “Our operational and financial transactions are in the open domain and our weekly newsletter always contains details of our activities and finances.” He described CAPS as one of the Board’s most revolutionary innovations. “With a system like CAPS, admissions into our institutions are transparent and anyone can question why a candidate is not admitted despite meriting it.” According to him, the notorious culture of secret or “under-the-table” admissions has largely become a thing of the past. “My belief is that transparency transforms institutions by eliminating toxic silos.” Partnerships That Strengthened the Institution Prof. Oloyede credited much of JAMB’s success to strategic partnerships with government agencies, tertiary institutions, security organisations, examination bodies, the media and over 1,010 private CBT centre owners. “We could not have achieved anything without leveraging networks and partnerships.” He acknowledged the cooperation of the National Security Adviser, the Director-General of the Department of State Services, the National Intelligence Agency, the Nigeria Police Force, NSCDC, EFCC, ICPC, NIMC, NCC, Vice Chancellors, Rectors, Provosts, civil society organisations and professional associations within and outside Nigeria. He also highlighted the establishment of the Nigerian Educational Assessment Academy (NEAA), created alongside 18 national agencies to train educational assessment professionals. “TEAM means Together Everyone Achieves More,” he said. “That became our mantra.” Gratitude to leaders, stakeholders Throughout his address, Oloyede repeatedly acknowledged those he said made JAMB’s transformation possible. He expressed gratitude to former President Muhammadu Buhari for appointing him, former President Olusegun Obasanjo for earlier identifying his leadership potential, and President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for retaining confidence in him. He also thanked Minister of Education Dr. Maruf Tunji Alausa, former Minister Prof. Tahir Mamman, Minister of State for Education Prof. Suwaiba Said Ahmad, Permanent Secretary Abel Enitan and former Permanent Secretary Sonny Echono. Several governors also received special recognition for donating land, office complexes, vehicles and Professional Test Centres across the country. Among those acknowledged were Prof. Babagana Zulum of Borno State, whose government built and donated the North-East Mega Professional Test Centre and named it after him; Nyesom Wike for providing office facilities and land in Rivers State within 24 hours of his request; Babatunde Raji Fashola for facilitating Certificates of Occupancy for JAMB properties; Ibikunle Amosun and Dapo Abiodun for supporting the South-West Mega Professional Test Centre project; Godwin Obaseki for relocating JAMB’s Edo office to a befitting site; Rochas Okorocha for land allocation in Imo State; Babajide Sanwo-Olu for allocating lands across Lagos State; AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq and Douye Diri for assisting JAMB’s facilities in Kwara and Bayelsa States. He also appreciated private individuals including Ahmad Raji (SAN) for donating a fully equipped Professional Test Centre in Iseyin and Dr. Wale Babalakin for repeatedly making the Bola Babalakin Hall available free of charge for JAMB’s annual policy meetings. The outgoing Registrar equally paid tribute to past Registrars, Governing Board members, directors, staff unions, retired employees, examination bodies, tertiary institutions, civil society groups, candidates, parents, security agencies, professional organisations and members of the media. “I seldom say it in order to keep you on your toes,” he told JAMB staff. “But I now say it loud: thank you very much.” A legacy beyond infrastructure Oloyede noted that beyond physical infrastructure, JAMB under his watch earned national and international recognition for accountability, technological innovation and service delivery. He disclosed that Prof. Emeritus Peter Okebukola had documented about 200 achievements recorded during the administration, while acknowledging the contributions of numerous academics and professionals who helped shape the Board’s reforms. “The story of JAMB is that of continuous progress,” he said, insisting that his administration merely built upon foundations laid by previous Registrars. Passing the baton Turning to his successor, Prof. Segun Aina, Oloyede expressed confidence that the Board’s future remains secure. “As I hand over the leadership of this great institution, I do so with absolute confidence in its future.” He described Aina as a younger ICT expert capable of taking JAMB to greater heights. “I wish my successor great success and his success is the success of all of us who have been privileged to steer JAMB since its inception.” “My belief is that the advantage and vibrancy of his younger age and his ICT expertise would propel the Board to higher heights than previously attained.” He pledged to remain available whenever his advice might be needed while urging Nigerians to support the new Registrar. “There is no success without a successor. They should rather support and pray for Prof. Aina’s success. It is time to face the future with renewed vigour.” A Personal Farewell As he prepared to leave office, the former Registrar became reflective, thanking his wife, children, grandchildren and close friends for standing by him throughout what he described as a demanding national assignment. “It is now over,” he said quietly. He concluded by once again committing JAMB’s future to God. “Finally, I thank Almighty Allah for the privilege of serving Nigeria through this noble institution. May He continue to guide, protect and bless the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board in the faithful discharge of its statutory responsibilities for generations to come.” With those words, Nigerians have witnessed one of the most consequential tenures in the history of JAMB—a decade marked by ambitious reforms, uncompromising accountability, digital transformation and an enduring insistence that institutional success is achieved not by one individual, but by collective purpose. The post History Made, Future Beckons: How Oloyede’s stewardship redefined JAMB, restored public trust appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Aswat Nissa lance une plateforme numérique sur le féminicide en Tunisie
items.description: Une plateforme numérique destinée à recenser, documenter et suivre les cas de féminicide en Tunisie, sera lancée par l’association féministe Aswat Nissa («Voix de femmes»), le 12 août 2026, à l’occasion de la présentation de son rapport annuel sur les féminicides pour l’année 2025. Selon l’organisation féministe, cette première plateforme électronique de ce type dans le pays vise à combler le manque de données officielles et de fournir un outil accessible aux chercheurs, aux médias et à la société civile. Cette initiative voit le jour dans un contexte qu’Aswat Nissa juge marqué par la persistance des meurtres de femmes, l’absence de statistiques officielles exhaustives et des lacunes dans les mécanismes de prévention et de protection. La plateforme devrait permettre de centraliser les informations sur les différents cas, d’en suivre l’évolution et de rendre les données plus facilement exploitables, notamment pour l’élaboration de politiques publiques de lutte contre les violences fondées sur le genre. À cette même occasion sera présenté le troisième rapport annuel de l’association sur ce phénomène, après ceux consacrés aux années 2023 et 2024. Selon le décompte déjà publié par Aswat Nissa au début de l’année, au moins 30 féminicides ont été enregistrés en Tunisie en 2025, contre 26 cas documentés en 2024. L’organisation a souligné à maintes reprises que le chiffre réel pourrait être plus élevé, en raison des difficultés d’accès à l’information et de l’absence de base de données publique complète. Le rapport sur l’année 2024 avait également mis en évidence la forte dimension familiale et conjugale du phénomène. Sur les 26 cas recensés, 36 % avaient été attribués aux maris des victimes, tandis que d’autres meurtres avaient été commis par des ex-partenaires, des fils, des pères ou d’autres membres de la famille. Seize cas avaient été enregistrés dans le Grand Tunis. Depuis 2017, la Tunisie dispose de la loi organique n° 58 relative à l’élimination de la violence à l’égard des femmes, considérée, au moment de son adoption, comme l’une des législations les plus avancées de la région. Toutefois, des organisations tunisiennes et internationales ont signalé, au fil des ans, des problèmes liés à sa mise en œuvre, notamment en ce qui concerne l’évaluation des risques, l’accès des victimes à des mesures de protection et la disponibilité de structures d’accueil. Aswat Nissa entend donc utiliser la nouvelle plateforme non seulement comme une base de données statistiques, mais aussi comme un outil de documentation et de plaidoyer visant à renforcer la prévention, la protection des femmes exposées à la violence et la responsabilité des institutions. Sa présentation est prévue à la veille de la Fête nationale de la femme tunisienne, célébrée chaque année le 13 août, date anniversaire de la promulgation, en 1956, du Code du statut personnel. I. B. Recrudescence inquiétante des féminicides en Tunisie L’article Aswat Nissa lance une plateforme numérique sur le féminicide en Tunisie est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: OIC welcomes Pak-Saudi-Turkiye joint defence pact, calls it 'important strategic step'
items.description: The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) has welcomed the signing of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye, terming it an “important strategic step”. The pact aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empowers the three states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them. In a statement posted on X, OIC Secretary General Hissein Brahim Taha expressed his “strong appreciation and support” for the agreement, describing it as an “important strategic step” that reflected the three countries’ commitment to strengthening regional and international cooperation. Taha said the agreement constitutes “a fundamental pillar for supporting security and stability in the region and across the Muslim world”. He added that it embodies a “shared resolve to address growing security challenges and strengthen solidarity and constructive partnerships” among the OIC member states. The OIC is the second largest organisation after the United Nations, with Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye among its 57 members. The OIC chief also praised the “tireless efforts and wise leadership” of the three countries that culminated in the signing of the “historic agreement”. He expressed hope that the pact would contribute to achieving peace and prosperity in the region and the wider international community. The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was signed on Friday at a trilateral summit in Makkah, pledging to strengthen collective security, deepen defence cooperation and promote peace and stability in the region and beyond. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan signed the pact during the “Makkah Al-Mukarramah Summit for Joint Defence”. Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif were also present at the signing ceremony. Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had already signed the “ Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement ” in Riyadh last September, pledging that any attack on either nation would be treated as an act of aggression against both. Saudi Arabia’s Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly has said the new tripartite agreement “does not supersede or replace any existing bilateral or multilateral agreements between these countries”. Meanwhile, the Turkish president said the pact targets no country and remains open to participation of other friendly nations seeking peace. PM Shehbaz undertook a three-day visit to Saudi Arabia from August 6 to 8, while Erdogan made a one-day trip to attend the summit. On Saturday morning, the prime minister paid a visit to Masjid-i-Nabvi in Madina. He then departed for Pakistan from the Madina airport, where he was seen off by Madina Governor Prince Salman bin Sultan Al Saud. PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, also a former foreign minister, hailed the agreement as a “significant milestone” in the country’s history. In a post on X, he noted that the pact was a “historic development that will further strengthen our defence capabilities”. “This agreement is not only a guarantee of a stable and secure future for Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye, but also a historic document for regional and global peace,” he emphasised. The PPP chairman also praised the roles of PM Shehbaz and CDF Munir “in making the agreement possible”. Bahrain, Somalia welcome pact In a statement issued by its foreign ministry, Bahrain welcomed the agreement as a “key addition to the broader regional defence architecture”. Bahrain said it viewed the pact as a “strategic partnership between equal partners, driven by a shared commitment to safeguard regional and global stability while bolstering credible deterrence”. The foreign ministry “highlighted the formidable defence capabilities and military expertise of the three nations, noting their proven track record in serving regional security, stability, and honouring international commitments”. The pact “complements and enhances the collective defence systems of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) through solidarity and strategic integration”, Bahrain noted. “Reaffirming that Saudi Arabia’s security is integral to its own, Bahrain expressed full support for all initiatives that protect national sovereignty, safeguard territorial integrity, and advance political solutions to regional issues,” the statement read. Somalia, whose defence minister paid a visit to Pakistan earlier this week, also congratulated the three signatories. In a statement, Somalia’s defence ministry termed the signing “a historic milestone in strengthening collective security, advancing defence cooperation, and building a strategic partnership capable of addressing shared security challenges”. The ministry expressed confidence that the agreement “will make a significant contribution to enhancing regional peace and stability”. While the signing of the agreement comes in the backdrop of heightened tensions in the Middle East arising from the US-Israel war on Iran, the pact was under deliberation months before the conflict began. The three countries, along with Egypt, have been closely involved in efforts to promote regional stability and contain the regional upheaval sparked by the US-Iran war.

items.title: Football : Gianni Infantino rattrapé par une affaire impliquant une ex-collaboratrice à l'UEFA
items.description: Le patron de la FIFA, Gianni Infantino, continue d'essuyer les attaques. Alors que celui-ci a recu le 7 août en Colombie le soutien de plusieurs acteurs du football sud-americain, The Telegraph a publie une enquete « approfondie » sur la relation qu'Infantino, « marie [depuis 2001] et pere de quatre enfants », aurait entretenu avec une « employee subalterne » lorsqu'il etait secretaire general de l'UEFA de 2009 a 2016. Au cours de cette relation, affirme le quotidien britannique, cette femme qui occupait initialement « un poste administratif » aurait connu une « ascension fulgurante » au sein de l'organisation. « M. Infantino aurait promu sa pretendue amante, lui accordant une augmentation de salaire de 30 % et un salaire d'environ 160 000 francs suisses », peut-on ainsi lire. Toutefois, precise encore The Telegraph , « la situation aurait degenere lorsque M. Platini l'a apprise ». « Elle ou toi ? », aurait un jour lance le patron de l'UEFA a son secretaire general, rapporte The Telegraph qui revendique s'etre « entretenu avec de nombreux temoins » au cours de son enquete, ce a quoi Infantino aurait repond « elle va partir ». Des allegations « totalement fausses », refute Infantino Celle-ci aurait par la suite obtenu, toujours selon la meme source, une indemnite de depart « a six chiffres », la encore grâce a l'intervention d'Infantino, « detournant ainsi des fonds de l'UEFA qui auraient pu etre consacres au football amateur». Par ailleurs, « dans le cadre de cet accord », l'UEFA, « a egalement finance […] les etudes de cette femme en MBA dans une ecole de commerce dont les frais de scolarite s'elevaient a environ 45 000 livres sterling par an », est-il precise. « Ce paiement etait conforme a la reglementation en vigueur a l'epoque pour les departs du personnel », a declare le 7 août un porte-parole de l'UEFA, cite par le quotidien britannique, reconnaissant un versement a cette femme. « Ces reglementations ont ete renforcees depuis 2016 et le reglement actuel du personnel – qui s'applique a tous les employes de l'UEFA, quel que soit leur niveau – reflete celui d'une organisation moderne et prestigieuse », a assure ce porte-parole. Du cote de la FIFA, un porte-parole a fait savoir que Gianni Infantino « refute categoriquement ces allegations, qui sont totalement fausses. Toute insinuation de comportement inapproprie ou de violation des statuts ou reglements est diffamatoire ».

items.title: Bougouriba/Lutte contre le paludisme : Les acteurs locaux mobilisés pour la première édition des Journées nationales de lutte anti-vectorielle
items.description: Bougouriba/Lutte contre le paludisme : Les acteurs locaux mobilisés pour la première édition des Journées nationales de lutte anti-vectorielle Diébougou, 7 août 2026 (AIB) – Les autorités administratives, sanitaires, coutumières, religieuses ainsi que les leaders d'opinion de la province de la Bougouriba ont pris part, le jeudi 6 août 2026 à Diébougou, à une rencontre de plaidoyer et de mobilisation en prélude à la première édition des Journées nationales de lutte anti-vectorielle (JNLAV). La rencontre était présidée par le Haut-commissaire de la province, Amidou Konaté, également président du Conseil de santé du district. Cette rencontre visait à susciter l'adhésion et l'engagement des différents acteurs en faveur de la campagne nationale de lutte contre le paludisme, qui se déroulera du 8 au 9 août 2026 dans la province. Selon les responsables sanitaires, l'objectif global des Journées nationales de lutte anti-vectorielle est de contribuer à la réduction de la transmission du paludisme à travers l'institutionnalisation d'actions régulières d'élimination des gîtes larvaires et d'assainissement durable du cadre de vie. Le Médecin-chef du district (MCD) sanitaire de Diébougou, Dr Faïssal Nikiéma, a rappelé que le paludisme demeure la première cause de morbidité et de mortalité dans les formations sanitaires, particulièrement en cette période d'hivernage, propice à la prolifération des moustiques. Pour lui, seule une forte mobilisation communautaire permettra de réduire efficacement l'impact de cette maladie. Dans la Bougouriba, les interventions retenues pour cette première édition portent notamment sur le curage des caniveaux, l'élimination des gîtes larvaires dans les espaces publics, la collecte et la gestion des pneus usagés ainsi que l'assainissement des dépôts sauvages d'ordures. Présidant la rencontre, le Haut-commissaire Amidou Konaté a invité l'ensemble des forces vives de la province à s'approprier cette initiative en participant activement aux activités programmées. « La lutte contre le paludisme est l'affaire de tous. Chaque citoyen doit poser des actes concrets pour assainir son environnement afin de protéger sa famille et sa communauté », a-t-il exhorté. Il a également appelé les autorités locales, les services techniques, les organisations communautaires et les leaders coutumiers et religieux à poursuivre les actions de sensibilisation afin d'assurer une forte participation des populations. À travers cette campagne, les autorités sanitaires entendent renforcer les mesures préventives et accélérer les efforts visant à faire reculer durablement le paludisme, avec pour ambition de l'éliminer comme problème majeur de santé publique au Burkina Faso à l'horizon 2030. Agence d'Information du Burkina KMG/ata

items.title: ‘There seems to be selective justice in some cases’ – Kofi Bentil
items.description: Senior lawyer and Vice President of IMANI Africa, Kofi Bentil, has raised concerns about what he describes as possible selective justice under the current government, arguing that the administration’s handling of prosecutions could give credence to claims of political bias. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, August 8, Mr Bentil said those accusing the government of selective justice had sufficient grounds to make their case, while acknowledging that those who disagreed could also present arguments in defence of the government. However, he said the government’s record over its four-year mandate would ultimately provide the strongest evidence. “This government, and by extension, this party, the NDC, will be judged after four years,” he said. According to Mr Bentil, two years into the administration, there were already grounds to argue that the government had been more aggressive in prosecuting people associated with the opposition while appearing more inclined to free or protect people within its own ranks. “To that extent, therefore, you can claim there is selective justice,” he said. Democracy under threat? Mr Bentil also raised concerns about the state of Ghana’s democracy, cautioning against waiting until democratic institutions and freedoms had been significantly weakened before taking action. “For me, I’m not waiting for all of our democracy to be removed from under our feet, for us to fall down before we rise up,” he said. He stressed the need for citizens to remain vigilant and work to protect and expand the democratic space. His comments come amid concerns raised at a recent ‘Democracy under attack demonstration’ by the NPP over alleged selective justice and what some protesters described as threats to Ghana’s democratic governance. Mr Bentil said one of the key messages of the demonstration was the need to draw attention to concerns that democracy could be under threat. He argued that if any government or president attempted to undermine democratic principles, citizens had a responsibility to resist and demand accountability. Mr Bentil also referred to calls for the fast-tracking of case involving former official of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), including the case of Wontumi matter. He said concerns had been raised that the cases were being accelerated with the ultimate objective of securing convictions and imprisonment. He maintained that the government’s actions over the remainder of its four-year term would provide the basis for assessing whether the allegations of selective justice were justified. Ultimately, he suggested, the strongest test would be whether similar standards of justice were applied to individuals on both sides of Ghana’s political divide.

items.title: We have to stay at the forefront and expand the frontiers of freedom – Kofi Bentil
items.description: Senior lawyer and Vice-President of IMANI Africa, Kofi Bentil, has urged Ghanaians to remain vigilant in protecting democratic freedoms, saying citizens should not wait until their rights have been eroded before taking action. Mr Bentil said the preservation of democracy requires continuous vigilance and a willingness to challenge developments that could undermine constitutional freedoms. “For me, I am not waiting for all of our democracy to be removed from under our feet and for us to fall down before we rise up,” he said. “So we always have to make sure that we are staying at the forefront and ensure that we expand the frontiers of freedom.” He made the comments while speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, in the aftermath of the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) “Democracy Under Attack” demonstration in Accra. Thousands of NPP members and supporters took to the streets on Thursday to protest what the party described as threats to Ghana’s democracy and the weakening of key state institutions under the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC). The demonstration culminated in the presentation of a petition at the forecourt of Jubilee House, the seat of government. The NPP delegation was led by Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin, General Secretary Osei Kyei-Mensah-Bonsu and the Chief of Staff to NPP flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia. The party had earlier submitted a separate petition to the Supreme Court. He acknowledged that there were arguments on both sides of the debate over whether selective justice exists in Ghana. “I think those arguing for selective justice will have enough facts to back what they are saying, but those who are also arguing that we don’t have selective justice will have their case too,” he said. However, he suggested that the ultimate assessment would come from the government’s record over its four-year mandate. “But the proof of the pudding is in its eating,” he said. According to Mr Bentil, the government and the governing NDC would ultimately be judged by the decisions and actions taken during its time in office. “This government and by extension this NDC party will be judged after four years,” he said. He noted that two years of the administration’s tenure had already elapsed, making it possible for citizens to begin assessing its record. “Two years have passed, if you draw the report card, there is ground to say that they have been more zealous in prosecuting people in the opposition and more zealous in freeing people from within their ranks,” he argued. He said this perception provided grounds for those who believe the justice system was being applied selectively to make their case. “And to that extent therefore, you can claim there is selective justice,” he said. For Mr Bentil, however, the debate should not be confined to determining whether democratic freedoms have already been lost. He warned against a situation in which citizens only react after institutions and constitutional protections have already been significantly weakened. He has previously argued that democratic decline can happen gradually, rather than through a single dramatic event. “When you see people demonstrating, whether you agree with them or not, first have the respect for the fact that they put themselves on the line to push the boundaries of our democracy,” he said. For Mr Bentil, the willingness of citizens to challenge authority is itself an important safeguard against the concentration of political power.

items.title: Kiev promet à Washington de ne plus attaquer un terminal pétrolier lié aux États-Unis, selon Bloomberg
items.description: L'Ukraine s'est engagee a ne pas frapper les infrastructures du Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC), ni certains navires se dirigeant vers son terminal en mer Noire, rapporte Bloomberg le 7 août en citant un responsable americain. Cet engagement a ete pris apres des discussions entre Kiev et de hauts responsables de l'administration americaine. L'engagement ne s'applique toutefois qu'a certains navires. Selon Bloomberg, les bâtiments concernes ne doivent appartenir ni a des personnes physiques ni a des entites russes, ne doivent pas figurer sur les listes de sanctions et ne doivent transporter ni petrole ni autres cargaisons russes. L'agence indique egalement que des canaux de communication ont ete ouverts avec les transporteurs afin d'identifier les navires concernes. La demarche americaine intervient apres plusieurs attaques de drones dans la region de Novorossiïsk. Selon Bloomberg, ces incidents ont contribue a la hausse des cours mondiaux du petrole, faisant du fonctionnement du terminal un sujet depassant largement le seul cadre du conflit russo-ukrainien. Une infrastructure internationale strategique Le consortium constitue avant tout le principal debouche du petrole kazakh vers les marches internationaux. Plus de 80 % des exportations petrolieres du Kazakhstan transitent par ce reseau, qui relie les champs de l'ouest du pays au terminal maritime situe sur la cote russe de la mer Noire, pres de Novorossiïsk. Long d'environ 1 500 kilometres et dote d'une capacite annuelle de 83 millions de tonnes, l'oleoduc joue ainsi un role majeur dans l'acheminement du brut kazakh vers les marches mondiaux. Son actionnariat souligne egalement le caractere international de l'infrastructure. Le consortium reunit des interets russes et kazakhs, mais aussi de grandes compagnies occidentales. Parmi ses principaux participants figurent la Russie via Transneft, le Kazakhstan via KazMunayGas, ainsi que Lukoil, Chevron, ExxonMobil et Shell. Le groupe americain Chevron detient 15 % du consortium. Les perturbations du reseau ont deja eu des consequences directes pour le Kazakhstan. Le ministere kazakh de l'energie a notamment constate une baisse de la production petroliere apres certaines interruptions. La diplomatie du pays a egalement condamne les frappes contre ces installations, estimant qu'elles portaient atteinte aux interets nationaux du Kazakhstan. Des attaques qui ont pousse Washington a intervenir Plusieurs incidents autour du terminal avaient precede les discussions entre Washington et Kiev. Le 30 juillet, deux tankers se trouvant a proximite des installations du consortium avaient notamment ete vises. Aucun deces ni fuite de carburant n'avait ete signale. Le consortium avait neanmoins rappele que ces attaques intervenaient malgre les appels du Kazakhstan et d'autres actionnaires etrangers a ne pas porter atteinte a cette infrastructure energetique internationale. Les consequences potentielles de ces frappes avaient egalement suscite des inquietudes aux etats-Unis. Le directeur general de Chevron, Mike Wirth, avait evoque aupres de la Maison Blanche les risques de dommages collateraux, alors que le groupe americain possede une participation importante dans le projet. L'administration du president americain Donald Trump avait ensuite averti Kiev de ne pas prendre pour cible les navires et les infrastructures petrolieres de pays tiers en mer Noire. Moscou avait pour sa part vivement condamne ces attaques contre les installations du consortium. Le 30 juillet, la porte-parole du ministere russe des Affaires etrangeres, Maria Zakharova, les avait qualifiees de « terrorisme » et avait denonce des frappes visant des infrastructures energetiques civiles.

items.title: 10 phones with the quality cameras in 2026, excluding iPhones
items.description: Smartphone cameras have become remarkably powerful, with manufacturers increasingly competing on sensor size, megapixel counts, optical zoom and computational photography. While Apple’s iPhones remain popular among mobile photographers, several Android manufacturers now offer phones with camera systems capable of capturing exceptional levels of detail. From Samsung and Xiaomi to OPPO, vivo and Honor, here are 10 phones with some of the sharpest cameras available in 2026. 1. OPPO Find X9 Ultra The OPPO Find X9 Ultra sits firmly among the most ambitious camera phones available. Its camera system is designed for photographers who want detail across different shooting situations, from standard photographs to distant subjects. Its combination of advanced sensors, powerful image processing and high-quality zoom makes it particularly attractive to users who want a phone capable of producing highly detailed images without relying on additional camera equipment. 2. Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra Samsung’s Ultra series has become synonymous with versatile smartphone photography, and the Galaxy S26 Ultra continues that approach. Its camera setup gives users several focal-length options, making it suitable for everything from everyday photography to portraits and long-distance shots. The phone is particularly impressive when it comes to zoom photography, allowing users to capture distant subjects while retaining a high level of detail. 3. Xiaomi 17 Ultra The Xiaomi 17 Ultra is another serious contender for photographers who prioritise image quality. Its large main camera sensor is designed to capture plenty of light and detail, while its telephoto system gives users greater flexibility when photographing distant subjects. For anyone looking for a flagship Android phone with an emphasis on photography, the Xiaomi 17 Ultra deserves consideration. 4. vivo X300 Pro vivo has increasingly positioned its flagship smartphones as camera-focused devices, and the X300 Pro is one of its strongest examples. The phone is particularly well suited to portrait and telephoto photography. Its camera processing helps preserve detail while producing images with strong colours and clarity, making it a compelling option for mobile photographers. 5. OPPO Find X9 Pro The OPPO Find X9 Pro combines flagship-level hardware with a camera system designed for detailed photographs. It is capable of producing sharp images in a variety of conditions, while its portrait and zoom capabilities add versatility. The device is especially appealing to users who want a premium camera experience alongside fast performance and modern Android features. 6. Huawei Pura 90s Pro Max Huawei’s Pura series has developed a reputation for putting photography at the centre of its flagship smartphones. The Pura 90s Pro Max follows that tradition with sophisticated camera hardware and a strong focus on zoom photography. Its high-resolution telephoto camera is particularly useful for capturing distant subjects with plenty of detail. 7. Honor Magic 8 Pro The Honor Magic 8 Pro is another Android flagship worth considering for photography. The phone’s camera system performs particularly well in challenging lighting conditions, where maintaining detail can be difficult for smartphone cameras. It also offers a versatile setup for users who want to shoot portraits, landscapes and distant subjects. 8. Xiaomi 17 Not everyone wants a huge smartphone, and the Xiaomi 17 offers a more compact option without abandoning flagship photography. Its camera system is capable of producing detailed photographs while maintaining a smaller overall footprint. For buyers who want a high-end camera phone that is easier to handle, the Xiaomi 17 is an interesting alternative. 9. Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra Foldable phones have traditionally lagged behind conventional flagships in camera hardware, but Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra takes a more ambitious approach. The device combines the large foldable display with a high-end camera system, making it useful for people who want both productivity and photography capabilities in one device. Its large screen can also make editing and reviewing photographs more convenient. 10. Xiaomi 15 Ultra Despite being an older model than some of the phones on this list, the Xiaomi 15 Ultra remains a formidable camera phone. Its large main sensor and high-resolution periscope telephoto camera give it excellent versatility, particularly for users who enjoy photographing distant subjects. It remains a strong choice for anyone who wants flagship-level smartphone photography without necessarily buying the newest model. items.title: Respect protesters whether you agree with them or not – Kofi Bentil tells Ghanaians
items.description: Senior lawyer and Vice-President of IMANI Africa, Kofi Bentil, has urged Ghanaians to respect citizens who take to the streets to demonstrate, even when they disagree with the protesters’ political views or demands. Mr Bentil said protesters and activists play a crucial role in defending democratic freedoms because they are often willing to put themselves on the line to challenge authority and push the boundaries of civic liberties. “When you see people demonstrating, whether you agree with them or not, first have the respect for the fact that they put themselves on the line to push the boundaries of our democracy,” he said. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, Mr Bentil was commenting in the wake of the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) “Democracy Under Attack” demonstration in Accra. Thousands of NPP supporters and party leaders took to the streets on Thursday to protest what the opposition party described as threats to Ghana’s democratic institutions under the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC). The demonstration culminated in the presentation of a petition at the forecourt of Jubilee House, the seat of government. The NPP delegation was led by Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin, General Secretary Osei Kyei-Mensah-Bonsu and the Chief of Staff to NPP flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia. The party had earlier submitted a separate petition to the Supreme Court. Mr Bentil’s principal message was that disagreement with the substance of a demonstration should not translate into disrespect for the people exercising their democratic rights. “You may not agree with them, but respect their activism,” he said. He argued that activists are an important part of the democratic process because their willingness to challenge those in authority helps ensure that citizens’ freedoms are not gradually restricted. “It is the activist you saw on the road who pushed the boundaries of freedom and democracy and make your liberty assured,” he said. For Mr Bentil, the value of activism lies partly in its ability to test the limits of political power. A demonstration may be inconvenient to the government or unpopular with sections of society, he suggested, but the act of protesting can nevertheless strengthen democracy by forcing institutions and those in authority to respond to public concerns. The NPP’s demonstration was organised under the theme “Democracy Under Attack” , with the party accusing the NDC government of undermining democratic principles and weakening key state institutions. The party mobilised a large crowd of supporters in Accra, with senior party figures joining the protest. At the end of the demonstration, the party presented a petition at Jubilee House after earlier submitting another petition to the Supreme Court. The NPP’s decision to take its concerns to the streets reflects its broader opposition to what it considers the excessive use of state power and the weakening of institutions that are supposed to protect constitutional democracy. The senior lawyer also warned that an attack on democracy does not necessarily arrive through a sudden or dramatic event. “When you talk about an attack on democracy, never in the history of mankind happens suddenly. It creeps on you as a nation,” he said. Mr Bentil referred to a lecture he delivered in Germany, where he discussed historical examples of democratic systems being weakened from within. He cited Adolf Hitler and Benito Mussolini, arguing that they used democratic principles and political processes to gain power before subsequently using laws and state institutions to undermine constitutionalism. “I was explaining to the white people that Hitler and Mussolini used democratic principle to enter office and then when they got into office, they used laws and other that are supposedly part of the democratic system to cancel out constitutionalism and the democracy they had,” he said. His broader warning was that citizens should not assume that democracy can only be threatened by an outright coup, the suspension of a constitution or the abolition of elections. According to him, democratic freedoms can also be eroded incrementally through actions that may initially appear isolated or insignificant. “And everywhere people had been oppressed, it starts slowly,” he added. Mr Bentil therefore urged Ghanaians to pay attention to developments that could gradually restrict civic freedoms or weaken institutions responsible for protecting constitutional rights. “We have a creeping situation which can get worse,” he warned. Mr Bentil also linked his defence of protesters to an experience he said he had during the NPP demonstration. He claimed that he was assaulted by police officers while attempting to get close to the gate of Jubilee House. “This is an improvement because I was beaten up. I had been attacked by policemen trying to get close to Jubilee House gate,” he said. For Mr Bentil, the experience reinforced the need to defend activism regardless of the political identity of those involved. His argument is that citizens should not have to support a particular political cause before being entitled to exercise their democratic rights. The IMANI Africa Vice-President emphasised that the protection of democratic rights cannot be conditional on public agreement with the protesters. “When you see people demonstrating, whether you agree with them or not, first have the respect for the fact that they put themselves on the line to push the boundaries of our democracy,” he said. The principle, he suggested, should apply equally to demonstrations organised by opposition parties, civil society groups, labour organisations or other sections of the public. If citizens are allowed to protest only when their cause is popular, then the right to protest becomes dependent on public approval rather than being treated as a constitutional freedom. Mr Bentil’s position is therefore that democratic tolerance requires people to distinguish between rejecting a protester’s message and respecting their right to express it. A person may disagree with the NPP’s assertion that Ghana’s democracy is under threat while still acknowledging the party’s right to organise a peaceful demonstration. Mr Bentil also raised concerns about what he described as selectivity in the administration of justice. He questioned why certain individuals appeared to be singled out for what he considered special treatment. “Today, there are questions of why are some people being singled out for that special treatment,” he said. “So I think as a matter of fact there is some selectivity in justice.” Mr Bentil’s warning about a “creeping situation” also places responsibility on citizens to recognise potential threats before they become entrenched. He argued that democratic decline often begins gradually, allowing societies to become accustomed to restrictions or institutional practices that might previously have been considered unacceptable. For that reason, he believes citizens should remain vigilant about the treatment of protesters, the conduct of security agencies, the independence of state institutions and the consistent application of justice. His appeal is for Ghanaians to recognise the importance of activism even when they disagree with the cause being advanced. “You may not agree with them, but respect their activism,” he said.

items.title: Rana Sanaullah says PML-N will form govt in AJK with two-thirds majority
items.description: Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah said on Saturday that the PML-N would form the government in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) with a two-thirds majority. He made the remarks while addressing a rally in Bagh ahead of the third phase of elections in the region. The third phase was originally slated to be held in Poonc Division, but will now only be held in its Bagh and Haveli districts due to law and order concerns. Addressing the rally, Sanaullah said that in the first two phases, the PML-N had secured 24 seats. He said that six more seats were required for a two-thirds majority government. He asserted that four more seats would be added following the August 10 polls, while five more would be added when polls would be held in the rest of Poonch Division. “The PML-N will form a government with a two-thirds majority. The people of Kashmir have trusted PML-N. They have trusted Mian Nawaz Sharif. They have trusted the development in Punjab,” he said. He urged supporters to show up and cast their votes on Monday to help PML-N secure a victory, promising that a PML-N government would prioritise development projects. He also said that the PML-N government would also meet with members of the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC). The JAAC, which has been demanding the abolishment of 12 seats in the local legislature reserved for refugees from Indian-held Kashmir, has been holding protests in the region for several weeks now. “When this government will be set up, with two-third majority, they will sit with [JAAC] representatives. Their first task will be to resolve this issue.” He said that 99 per cent of JAAC protesters were “our brothers”, adding that they were patriotic Kashmiris and Pakistanis. He added that the remainder were focused on creating divisions within the nation. He urged cooperation between a future PML-N government and the people of AJK in “exposing and defeating” those divisive elements. “We will defeat them and we will make Kashmir prosperous,” Sanaullah said. He further added that in the past, all large-scale development projects in AJK were only completed when the PML-N was in power in the Centre and in the region. He urged the people of Bagh to go out and vote on Monday, stressing that “all of Bagh should be involved in the government”. He added that PML-N founder Nawaz Sharif would fulfill his promises to the people of AJK by nominating one of the three PML-N candidates in Bagh as the future prime minister of AJK. Sanaullah added that Nawaz has already mentioned that he would sit down with the future AJK prime minister to discuss development projects in the region.

items.description: Boulgou/ offensive agro-pastorale : les VDP agricoles de Niaogho s'engagent à produire 10 tonnes de Niébé Niaogho, 4 août 2026 (AIB) – les VDP agricoles de la commune de Niaogho, province du Boulgou, projettent une récolte de plus de 10 tonnes de Niébé au terme de la campagne agricole 2026, grâce à l'appui conséquent en semences pour contribuer activement à l'autosuffisance alimentaire au Burkina Faso La dynamique d’autosuffisance alimentaire amorcée au Burkina Faso trouve un écho favorable dans la province du Boulgou. À Niaogho, les VDP agricoles se sont mobilisés pour faire de la présente campagne un succès de production. Saluant l’engagement du chef de l’État, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, les acteurs locaux ont exprimé leur satisfaction face à l'appui institutionnel reçu. Ce matériel et ces intrants doivent leur permettre de concrétiser leurs ambitions sur le terrain. « Nous avons reçu 120 kg de semences de niébé de 70 jours (variété Komkalé ), 150 kg de maïs d'un cycle de 85 jours ( variété barka), 1 kg de gombo, deux bâches, un semoir électronique et un pulvérisateur », a détaillé Assétou Sinka, vice-présidente des VDP agricoles de Niaogho. Forte de cet équipement, l’organisation entend honorer la confiance placée en elle par les autorités nationales. Le cap est désormais fixé : dépasser le seuil des 10 tonnes de niébé récoltées à la fin de la saison. La camarade Assetou Sinka a déclaré que, quelques défis subsistent pour garantir le rendement des cultures à cycle plus long. « »Compte tenu de l'avancement de la saison des pluies et de la durée de maturation du maïs (85 jours), nous demandons un appui complémentaire en engrais MPK , des herbicides pour éviter que les aléas pluviométriques ne compromettent la récolte. » » Malgré ces contraintes, l’enthousiasme reste intact au sein du groupe, qui a réitéré toute sa reconnaissance envers le gouvernement pour cet accompagnement stratégique dans le développement agropastoral local. Agence d'information du Burkina AA/SM/ata

items.title: Tarification des soins : les médecins du privé réclament une révision devenue urgente
items.description: La tarification nationale de référence (TNR) est de nouveau sur la table. Vingt ans après son adoption, les professionnels de santé estiment que ce barème n'est plus en phase avec le coût réel des soins. Ce décalage pèse directement sur le porte-monnaie des assurés, dont une partie finit par renoncer à se soigner. Parmi les chantiers les plus attendus de la réforme de l'Assurance maladie obligatoire (AMO) figure l'actualisation de la tarification nationale de référence. Les médecins du secteur privé pressent le gouvernement de réviser un dispositif resté inchangé depuis 2006. C'est pourtant ce barème qui sert toujours de base au calcul des remboursements de la CNSS, de la CNOPS et des autres organismes d'assurance maladie. Un barème inchangé depuis vingt ans Pour le Dr Tayeb Hamdi, médecin et chercheur en politiques et systèmes de santé, le débat ne porte pas uniquement sur les honoraires des praticiens. Il rappelle que la convention conclue en 2006 entre le ministère de la Santé, l'Agence nationale de l'assurance maladie (ANAM), les caisses d'assurance et les représentants des professions libérales prévoyait une révision de la TNR tous les trois ans. Une disposition qui n'a pourtant jamais été appliquée. Aujourd'hui, les consultations, les examens radiologiques et les médicaments sont facturés selon les tarifs pratiqués en 2026, tandis que les remboursements continuent d'être calculés sur la base de montants fixés il y a près de vingt ans. La différence reste à la charge des assurés. Le Dr Tayeb Hamdi rappelle, dans une déclaration à Hespress FR , qu'un affilié à la CNSS supporte encore 50,2 % des dépenses de soins ambulatoires, contre 41,1 % pour un assuré de la CNOPS. Plus globalement, en tenant compte de l'ensemble des dépenses de santé, remboursables ou non, les ménages financent près des deux tiers de leurs frais médicaux. Pour le spécialiste, cette situation a des conséquences directes sur les patients. Il relève que 41,5 % des Marocains renoncent aux soins. Ce taux atteint encore 36 % chez les personnes disposant pourtant d'une couverture maladie. De nombreux patients repoussent leurs consultations ou interrompent leur suivi médical en raison du reste à charge. Certaines maladies chroniques, comme le diabète, évoluent alors vers des complications plus lourdes, plus coûteuses et plus difficiles à prendre en charge. Le Dr Tayeb Hamdi note en ce sens que les dépenses de santé deviennent « catastrophiques » lorsqu'elles dépassent 10 % du budget d'un ménage, un seuil susceptible de fragiliser durablement une famille après une hospitalisation ou une maladie grave. Des remboursements de plus en plus éloignés de la réalité Les praticiens constatent également, au quotidien, le décalage entre les remboursements et les honoraires pratiqués. À ce sujet, le Dr Neima Kheiyali, kinésithérapeute, rappelle que les grilles utilisées par les organismes d'assurance maladie ont très peu évolué depuis 2006. Elle cite l'exemple d'une consultation de médecine générale toujours remboursée sur la base de 80 dirhams, ou d'une consultation spécialisée calculée sur la base de 150 dirhams, alors que les cabinets privés pratiquent généralement des honoraires compris entre 200 et 300 dirhams, pouvant atteindre 400 à 500 dirhams dans certaines spécialités, notamment en psychiatrie. Selon elle, l'inflation enregistrée ces dernières années a encore accentué cet écart, au détriment des patients. Dans le même sens, le Dr Tayeb Hamdi estime que « la révision de la tarification nationale de référence est devenue indispensable. L'objectif est de rapprocher les remboursements du coût réel des soins, de réduire le reste à charge des assurés et de limiter le renoncement aux soins ». Les prochains arbitrages du gouvernement seront suivis de près, tant par les professionnels de santé que par les bénéficiaires de l'AMO. Derrière les grilles tarifaires et les pourcentages se cachent des consultations reportées, des traitements interrompus et des maladies qui s'aggravent faute de moyens. C'est à cette réalité que se mesurera la réforme : non pas seulement à l'aune d'un nouveau barème, mais à la capacité des Marocains à accéder aux soins sans que leur situation financière constitue un obstacle. The post Tarification des soins : les médecins du privé réclament une révision devenue urgente appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Elhadj Bobo Barry de la FECATRAG : « Nous avons besoin du Président Doumbouya pour le bien de notre peuple »
items.description: Connu pour ses nombreuses sorties médiatiques en soutien aux actions gouvernementales notamment dans le secteur portuaire et de transit, le Secrétaire administratif de la FECATRAG, Elhadj Bobo Barry a affirmé que le peuple de Guinée a plus que jamais besoin du Président de la République pour le bien de sa jeunesse, la bonne marche des affaires et pour le bien être du peuple en Général. Cette déclaration du Secrétaire administratif de la Fédération des Commissionnaires agrées et Transitaires de Guinée intervient en un moment où les commentaires sur les congés annuels du Président Doumbouya en Grèce vont bon train. C’est dans cette optique qu’il a tenu à rappeler les nombreux bienfaits des actions du Président dans la décongestion du Port de Conakry et sur la fluidité des affaires en Guinée. Face à la crise de congestion qui avait frappé pendant un certain temps le Port Autonome de Conakry, le Président de la République, le Général Mamadi Doumbouya , a vait pris une mesure exceptionnelle en ordonnant la suspension de toutes les surestaries pour la période allant du 15 décembre 2025 au 31 janvier 2026 puis l’ a prorogé par la suite jusqu’au 31 mars 2026. L’annonce de cette décision à l’époque par le Ministre Porte-parole du Gouvernement, Ousmane Gaoual Diallo, avait suscité un soulagement sans précédent chez les acteurs économiques aux dires d u , Secrétaire administratif de la FECATRAG . Un « ouf de soulagement » pour l’import-export Pour Elhadj Bobo Barry, cette mesure était venue à point nommé pour préserver la santé financière des entreprises guinéennes: « Cette décision du Président de la République a été un grand ouf de soulagement pour tous les acteurs évoluant dans l’import et l’export. Il faut rappeler que ce n’ était pas une première. Soucieux de la santé économique de notre pays, le Chef de l’État avait déjà pris des dispositions pour désengorger le port. » Il souligne par ailleurs que cette saturation était a conséquence directe du dynamisme économique de la Guinée : « Depuis trois ans, le boom économique fait que notre port est saturé, mais cela n’empêche pas les opérateurs de venir faire des affaires ici. » Amélioration de la fluidité portuaire Selon le Secrétaire administratif de la ‘’ Fédération des Commissionnaires agrées et Transitaires de Guinée'’ , les réformes précédentes avaient déjà porté leurs fruits, notamment par l’élargissement des zones de débarquement des conteneurs vides et les pressions exercées sur les sociétés de consignation pour accélérer l’évacuation des marchandises. Cette gestion rigoureuse attire désormais les pays voisins sans façade maritime. « Des pays continentaux tels que le Mali, le Burkina et même le Niger cherchent à utiliser notre port, car ils y voient de la sérénité et du sérieux. Dans le monde des affaires, ce sont les clés de la prospérité », affirme-t-il. L’impact direct des décisions présidentielles sur le panier de la ménagère Expliquant l’aspect technique, Elhadj Bobo Barry rappelle que les surestaries sont des pénalités financières payées aux armateurs lorsqu’un conteneur dépasse le délai de franchise au port. « Ces charges supplémentaires sont extrêmement coûteuses et imprévues pour les importateurs. Elles s’ajoutent aux droits de douane, aux frais de consignation et de manutention. Lorsqu’un opérateur subit ces surcoûts, il est obligé de les répercuter sur le prix de vente, ce qui impacte directement le consommateur final. » En suspendant ces frais, le Président Doumbouya protège donc indirectement le pouvoir d’achat des Guinéens et favorise automatiquement : – l’ Allègement des frais de stationnement – La d élivrance rapide des bons – Le r établissement de la fluidité de circulation des marchandises. – La circulation permanente des gros porteurs – La livraison régulière des marchandises . A conclu Elhadj Bobo, qui estime que de tels chefs, méritent les prières de son peuple pour la continuité de ses actions salvatrice. Amadou Sylla L’article Elhadj Bobo Barry de la FECATRAG : « Nous avons besoin du Président Doumbouya pour le bien de notre peuple » est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Bissiga : 22 plants mis en terre par la CEB de Bissiga au nom de la résilience
items.description: Bissiga : 22 plants mis en terre par la CEB de Bissiga au nom de la résilience Bissiga, 06 août 2026 (AIB)-Le personnel de la Circonscription d'éducation de base (CEB) de Bissiga dans la province du Boulgou, conduit par le Chef de circonscription, Michel Boundaogo, a mis en terre 22 plants, ce jeudi 06 août 2026, à l'école Bissiga « A », à l'école Bissiga « C » et au sein de la CEB. Cette activité s'inscrit en soutien à l'initiative présidentielle pour la reconquête du couvert végétal. Selon le représentant du président de la délégation spéciale, Charles Delma, 2e vice-président, cette action vise à offrir un cadre d'apprentissage et de travail plus agréable aux élèves et aux enseignants. Il a saisi l'occasion pour inviter les autres chefs de service à emboîter le pas afin de reverdir les services et l'ensemble de la commune. Pour le Chef de la Circonscription d'éducation de base (CCEB) de Bissiga, Michel Boundaogo, cette initiative citoyenne est une première pour sa structure. « Nous ne comptons pas nous arrêter en si bon chemin. Nous allons pérenniser l'initiative et l'étendre à toutes les autres écoles de la circonscription. C'est à nous de montrer l'exemple pour inciter les directeurs d'écoles à suivre », a-t-il déclaré. Il a salué l'accompagnement de ses proches collaborateurs, notamment les inspecteurs et l'ensemble du personnel de la CEB. Le représentant des bénéficiaires, Théodore Delma, président du Conseil d'école de Bissiga « A », a salué l'initiative et remercié les donateurs pour ce geste écocitoyen. « Nous prenons l'engagement d'entretenir et de protéger ces arbres pour le bonheur de nos enfants », a-t-il affirmé. Le chef du service départemental de l'Environnement, le lieutenant Bassori Dissa, a insisté, quant à lui, sur la nécessité d'assurer le suivi des plants. « Nous encourageons le suivi de ces plants afin qu'ils puissent bien se développer pour le bonheur de tous, en particulier des élèves des écoles bénéficiaires », a-t-il exhorté. C'est dans une ambiance conviviale que les acteurs se sont séparés, en se donnant rendez-vous l'année prochaine pour évaluer le taux de survie des plants mis en terre. Agence d'Information du Burkina BW/SM/ata

items.title: Gov. Alia announces plans to close IDP camps in Benue
items.description: Gov. Hyacinth Alia has announced plans to close some Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) camps in Benue as a result of improved security in the state. Alia made the announcement during a media chat with the Renewed Hope Ambassadors Presidential Media Team, led by Mr Bayo Onanuga, the President’s Special Adviser on Media and Strategy. The News Agency of Nigeria(NAN) reports that the team is in Benue to inspect completed and ongoing Federal Government and state infrastructure projects across the 23 Local Government Areas (LGAs) of the state. Alia said improved security, supported by Federal Government intervention, had created relative peace, enabling many displaced persons to voluntarily return home and resume farming. He said security indices were being monitored through security agencies deployed across the LGAs, traditional institutions and residents, who provided useful information on developments within their communities. The governor recalled that 15 IDP camps had been established across the state following attacks and displacement. He, however, noted that the improved security situation was gradually changing the narrative. “We are already making some plans to close down some because the IDP occupants have voluntarily gone back to do their farming,” Alia said. He said the state government was working with the international community, including the United Nations and International Organisation for Migration (IOM), to achieve sustainable solutions for displaced persons. According to him, the objective is not merely to return displaced persons to their farms, only for them to flee again, but to create conditions that would enable them remain safely in their communities. Alia said the declining number of residents in the camps was encouraging, noting that many returnees were not only farming but also rebuilding their houses in their ancestral communities. He expressed optimism that sustained security efforts would enable the returnees to remain home, rebuild their livelihoods and contribute to the agricultural economy for which Benue is widely known. The governor said his administration declared a state of emergency on road infrastructure, resulting in improved connectivity across several parts of the state. He added that urban renewal projects were ongoing, while arterial roads in major townships had been reconstructed or upgraded to improve movement and economic activities. Alia also highlighted reforms in the primary education sector, saying hundreds of local government primary schools that had suffered years of neglect were being rehabilitated and returned to functionality. He said his administration had recruited 9,700 teachers for primary schools, describing the intervention as part of efforts to strengthen basic education across the state.. On healthcare, Alia said the state had revamped primary healthcare facilities while transforming the teaching hospital to a standard that now attracted patients from neighbouring states. He said the teaching hospital had attracted medical tourists from surrounding states, partly because of the availability of specialists and a VIP wing that had become popular among patients. The governor disclosed that medical equipment ordered through collaboration with U.S. government and subnational authorities was expected in the state for distribution to primary healthcare facilities across the LGAs. Alia said the administration had closely monitored its commitments to the people, stressing that political promises must be matched with deliberate action and measurable results.. He expressed appreciation to the Federal Government for its support, saying the completion of infrastructure projects was essential for citizens to experience and appreciate the dividends of democracy. Speaking at a dinner hosted by the state government after the media chat, Onanuga thanked Alia and his deputy, Samuel Ode, for the hospitality extended to the team. Onanuga said he invited senior media practitioners to witness firsthand the infrastructure development and transformation being undertaken by the Federal and Benue governments. He particularly commended the governor for reviving moribund facilities, including the Tarakum Mill, Otobi Water Works and the state brewery, describing the projects as catalysts for economic development. The presidential spokesperson also praised the administration for road development, particularly in remote and previously insecure areas, as well as its payment of teachers’ salaries and retirees’ benefits inherited from the previous administration. (NAN) The post Gov. Alia announces plans to close IDP camps in Benue appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Tunisie | Inquiétude dans le secteur du marbre et du granit
items.description: Les entreprises tunisiennes du secteur du marbre et du granit redoutent des redressements fiscaux rétroactifs portant sur une période allant jusqu’à 10 ans et exigent des éclaircissements urgents de l’administration fiscale. Le différend ne porte pas sur l’instauration d’un nouvel impôt, mais sur les modalités d’application d’une taxe prévue de longue date par la législation et, surtout, sur la possibilité d’en exiger le paiement au titre d’exercices antérieurs. Dans une lettre adressée le 3 août 2026 au directeur général des impôts et signée par le président de la chambre professionnelle, Taoufik Ben Saâd, les industriels ont signalé des contrôles fiscaux susceptibles d’entraîner des redressements couvrant jusqu’à dix années en arrière. Ce droit de consommation trouve son fondement juridique dans la loi tunisienne n° 88-62 du 2 juin 1988. Le texte stipule que les produits figurant dans le tableau annexé sont soumis à cette taxe, qu’ils soient importés ou fabriqués localement. La réglementation a été modifiée et complétée à plusieurs reprises par la suite. La question soulevée par les opérateurs concerne donc le périmètre des produits visés, l’assiette de calcul, le moment de l’imposition et, surtout, la réclamation de sommes relatives à des années durant lesquelles, selon la catégorie de produits, la taxe n’avait pas été concrètement appliquée aux ventes des producteurs. Pour les entreprises, un redressement portant sur plusieurs exercices aurait un impact particulièrement lourd, dans la mesure où la taxe n’avait pas été répercutée sur les prix pratiqués auprès des clients. Les sommes réclamées devraient donc être directement absorbées par les bilans des entreprises, auxquelles pourraient s’ajouter des charges supplémentaires liées aux pénalités et aux intérêts de retard. Les industriels redoutent par ailleurs une hausse du prix du marbre local ainsi qu’une perte de compétitivité face aux matériaux alternatifs utilisés dans la construction et les revêtements. Ce litige concerne une filière fortement implantée dans les régions intérieures du pays. Une étude récente de l’Office de développement du Nord-Ouest sur la filière du marbre à Siliana, fondée sur des données de l’Institut national de la statistique, indique qu’en 2024, les exportations de la catégorie de marbre analysée ont atteint environ 3,68 millions de kilogrammes, pour une valeur de 5,87 millions de dinars (1,77 million d'euros). La même étude met en évidence, parmi les problèmes structurels du secteur, la complexité des procédures d’ouverture de carrières, les délais d’obtention des autorisations ainsi que la nécessité de renforcer la formation, la transformation industrielle et les capacités d’exportation. Pour les professionnels du marbre et du granit, la priorité est désormais d’obtenir une position claire de l’administration fiscale définissant les modalités et la période d’application du droit de consommation, afin d’éviter — selon eux — que l’incertitude fiscale ne compromette les investissements et la continuité de la production des entreprises. I. B. L’article Tunisie | Inquiétude dans le secteur du marbre et du granit est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Ghana’s democracy is under a ‘creeping’ threat – Kofi Bentil warns
items.description: Senior lawyer and Vice-President of IMANI Africa, Kofi Bentil, has warned that attacks on democracy rarely happen abruptly, arguing that the gradual erosion of constitutional freedoms and institutions could pose a serious threat to Ghana’s democratic stability. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, August 8, Mr Bentil said democratic systems could be weakened from within when laws and state institutions are gradually used in ways that undermine constitutionalism. His comments followed Thursday’s “Democracy Under Attack” demonstration organised by the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) in Accra. Thousands of NPP supporters and party officials took to the streets to protest what the party described as threats to Ghana’s democratic institutions under the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) administration. The demonstration ended with the NPP presenting a petition at the forecourt of Jubilee House, the seat of government. The party’s delegation was led by Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin, General Secretary Osei Kyei-Mensah-Bonsu and the Chief of Staff to NPP flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia. The NPP had also earlier submitted a separate petition to the Supreme Court. Against this backdrop, Mr Bentil urged Ghanaians not to dismiss concerns about democratic backsliding simply because they emerge through isolated incidents. According to Mr Bentil, the erosion of democracy is often a gradual process which can be difficult to detect until institutions have already been significantly weakened. “When you talk about an attack on democracy, never in the history of mankind happens suddenly. It creeps on you as a nation,” he said. He referred to historical examples to illustrate his argument, recalling a lecture he delivered in Germany on the dangers of democratic backsliding. Mr Bentil said Adolf Hitler and Benito Mussolini were able to use democratic principles and political processes to gain power before subsequently using state structures and laws to dismantle constitutional safeguards. “I was explaining to the white people that Hitler and Mussolini used democratic principles to enter office and then when they got into office, they used laws and other [things] that are supposedly part of the democratic system to cancel out constitutionalism and the democracy they had,” he said. His argument was that democratic decline does not necessarily begin with the outright abolition of elections or the formal suspension of a constitution. Rather, it can start when institutions, laws and established democratic practices are gradually manipulated or weakened. “And everywhere people had been oppressed, it starts slowly,” he added. The IMANI Africa Vice-President also defended the role of activists and protesters in safeguarding democratic freedoms. He argued that citizens should respect people who participate in demonstrations even when they disagree with their political views or the specific demands of their protests. “It is the activist you saw on the road who pushed the boundaries of freedom and democracy and make your liberty assured,” he said. Mr Bentil said activism should not be judged solely on whether the public agrees with the message being advanced. “When you see people demonstrating, whether you agree with them or not, first have the respect for the fact that they put themselves on the line to push the boundaries of our democracy,” he said. “You may not agree with them, but respect their activism.” Mr Bentil said the current concerns should not be ignored because democratic decline, in his view, often occurs incrementally. “We have a creeping situation which can get worse,” he warned. For Mr Bentil, vigilance is particularly important because once restrictions on democratic freedoms become normalised, reversing them can become increasingly difficult. Mr Bentil also spoke about his own experience during the NPP demonstration. He claimed that he was assaulted by police officers while attempting to get close to the Jubilee House gate. “This is an improvement because I was beaten up. I had been attacked by policemen trying to get close to Jubilee House gate,” he said. Mr Bentil used the incident to reinforce his argument that activism and peaceful protest remain important safeguards within a democracy. His position is that even when a demonstration is politically contentious, the fundamental rights of those participating should be respected. The senior lawyer also raised concerns about what he described as apparent selectivity in the administration of justice. He questioned why certain individuals appeared to receive “special treatment” in circumstances where others might face different consequences. “Today, there are questions of why are some people being singled out for that special treatment,” he said. “So I think as a matter of fact there is some selectivity in justice.”
