items.title: Tenkodogo: La DPAERAH accueille la cérémonie tournante de montée des couleurs nationales
items.description: Tenkodogo: La DPAERAH accueille la cérémonie tournante de montée des couleurs nationales Tenkodogo, 5 août 2026 [AIB] – Le Haut-commissaire de la province du Boulgou, Constantin Dabiré, a présidé mercredi à Tenkodogo, la cérémonie tournante de montée des couleurs nationales à la Direction provinciale de l'Agriculture, de l'Eau, des Ressources Animales et Halieutiques [DPAERAH]. La cérémonie s'est déroulée en présence des corps constitués, des forces de défense et de sécurité [FDS] et des acteurs du développement local. A l'issue de la montée des couleurs, le Directeur provincial de l'agriculture de l'eau des ressources animales et halieutique Issa PABGO a présenté les missions et les attributions de sa structure. Il a traduit sa gratitude au Haut-commissaire pour le choix porté sur son sa direction pour abriter cette édition. Le Directeur provincial a ensuite dressé le bilan des activités en cours dans les secteurs de l'agriculture, de l'eau et de l'élevage. Il a évoqué, entre autres, les travaux d'entretien des cultures, les avancées enregistrées dans le domaine de l'élevage avec l'introduction de génisses gestantes importées du Brésil par un promoteur basé dans la commune de Zonsé, ainsi que les perspectives de la campagne agricole en cours. Il a également annoncé qu'une fin tardive de la saison des pluies est envisagée dans la région du Nakambé. Prenant la parole, le Haut-commissaire a salué les efforts des acteurs du monde rural dans la mise en œuvre des initiatives gouvernementales en faveur de la souveraineté alimentaire. Il a rappelé que les actions entreprises dans l'agriculture, l'eau et l'élevage s'inscrivent dans la politique nationale de renforcement de l'autosuffisance alimentaire. Le Camarade DABIRE a félicité les acteurs provinciaux pour les résultats engrangés au cours du mois de juillet, notamment dans la conduite de l'immersion patriotique obligatoire et pour les contributions en espèces et en nature mobilisées au profit de cette initiative. Il a, par ailleurs, remercié les partenaires techniques et financiers, les organisations intervenant dans les secteurs de l'agriculture et de l'élevage, ainsi que les étudiants présents. Pour sa part, le représentant de la Direction provinciale de la Police nationale [DPPN] a sensibilisé les participants sur le E-verbalisation, une innovation du ministère de la Sécurité lancée le 1er août 2026 à Ouagadougou, en vue de renforcer la répression des infractions au Code de la route. Il a précisé que la phase pilote concerne actuellement les véhicules à quatre roues et vise notamment le non-port de la ceinture de sécurité, l'excès de vitesse, l'usage du téléphone au volant et le non-respect des feux tricolores. Il a invité les usagers à respecter la limitation de vitesse fixée à 50 km/h en agglomération. La cérémonie a pris fin par la visite des stands d'exposition de produits locaux et des parcelles d'expérimentation et d'étude exploitées par les stagiaires de la DPAERAH. items.title: US Senate confirms Trump’s ex-lawyer Blanche as attorney general
items.description: President Donald Trump’s former personal lawyer Todd Blanche was confirmed as US attorney general on Saturday after Senate Republicans shrugged off Democratic concerns over politicization of the Justice Department. Blanche, who has already been serving as the top US law enforcement officer in an acting capacity, represented Trump as his private attorney in several criminal trials before entering government. The Senate, which Republicans narrowly control, confirmed him by 50 votes to 49. Trump, who has upended US political norms by seeking to bring nominally independent government agencies under his increasingly direct control, calls Blanche a “star.” Democrats opposed Blanche from the beginning, accusing Trump of turning the Department of Justice into a political weapon. “The attorney general is supposed to be the people’s lawyer,” Senator Dick Durbin, the ranking Democrat on the Senate Judiciary Committee, said on Tuesday. “Mr Blanche continues to operate as the president’s personal lawyer, treating the Justice Department like a law firm serving one client — the president.” There were doubts over whether the White House could persuade a handful of Republican holdouts, without whom even the narrow confirmation would have been impossible. The main sticking point was an attempt to establish a $1.8 billion fund for what Trump calls victims of politicized prosecutions, likely including the rioters who stormed the US Capitol on January 6, 2021 in an attempted insurrection to prevent Joe Biden from being certified as president after his defeat of Trump in the 2020 election. The other main issue was an extraordinary proposal granting immunity to Trump from tax audits. – ‘Hush money’ – Blanche ultimately defused the internal party opposition with a written order over the weekend scrapping the so-called political “anti-weaponization fund” and saying that the audit immunity agreement with Trump, his two eldest sons and the Trump Organization would only apply “retroactively” to past tax years and not future filings. Blanche has been serving as acting attorney general since Trump fired Pam Bondi, another political loyalist, in April. Since then, he has been closely tied to what Democrats dub a Trump “retribution” campaign against the 80-year-old president’s opponents. Blanche has also come in for criticism from victims of Jeffrey Epstein over his handling of the release of investigative files about the convicted sex offender, a one-time close friend of Trump. Prior to joining the Department of Justice, Blanche represented Trump in his New York trial over alleged “hush money” paid to porn star Stormy Daniels. He was also on the legal defense team in two federal cases brought against Trump by special counsel Jack Smith — for allegedly mishandling classified documents after leaving the White House and for seeking to overturn the results of the 2020 presidential election. Both cases were dropped after Trump won the 2024 presidential election. AFP The post US Senate confirms Trump’s ex-lawyer Blanche as attorney general appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: La Colombie reconnaît la souveraineté du Maroc sur son Sahara
items.description: La Colombie a annoncé un changement de sa position sur la question du Sahara et affirmé sa reconnaissance de la souveraineté du Royaume du Maroc sur ses Provinces du Sud. Cette nouvelle position a été annoncée, vendredi, lors de l’entretien qu’a eu le ministre des Affaires étrangères, de la Coopération africaine et des Marocains résidant à l’étranger, Nasser Bourita, avec le vice-président de la République de Colombie, José Manuel Restrepo, auquel a pris part le ministre des Relations extérieures, Omar Bula Escobar. Bula Escobar a, à cette occasion, affirmé que la Colombie « reconnaît la souveraineté du Maroc sur son Sahara », consacrant ainsi une nouvelle orientation de la position colombienne sur cette question. Pour sa part, Restrepo a souligné que cette annonce marque « un nouveau départ » dans les relations entre la Colombie et le Maroc, affirmant que le Royaume est « le premier allié de la Colombie en Afrique ». Il a, dans ce sens, exprimé la volonté de son pays d’établir avec le Maroc un partenariat stratégique. De son côté, Bourita a qualifié d ’ »historique » la décision de la Colombie de retirer sa reconnaissance de la pseudo RASD et de reconnaitre la souveraineté du Maroc sur son Sahara, soulignant qu’elle est susceptible de donner « un grand élan » aux relations bilatérales. Il a aussi précisé que le Maroc et la Colombie peuvent constituer des plateformes économiques l’un pour l’autre, en mettant à profit leurs positions respectives en Afrique et en Amérique latine. Bourita a, enfin, affirmé que sa présence à Cali, sur très hautes instructions du Roi Mohammed VI, pour représenter le Souverain à la cérémonie d’investiture du nouveau président Abelardo de la Espriella, traduit la volonté du Royaume d’accompagner cette nouvelle dynamique et de porter les relations maroco-colombiennes à un niveau supérieur. The post La Colombie reconnaît la souveraineté du Maroc sur son Sahara appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Algérie – France : le commerce bilatéral dégringole sous les 9 milliards €
items.description: Le commerce entre l’Algérie et la France continue de dégringoler. Dans un contexte de crise qui a duré près de deux ans, les échanges entre les deux pays ont encore baissé en glissement annuel pour passer sous la barre des 9 milliards d’euros contre 11 milliards en 2024 et 9,3 milliards en 2025. Des deux côtés, aucun secteur n’a réalisé une croissance. La baisse est générale. En plus de la crise politique entre les deux pays, cette dégringolade coïncide avec les mesures draconiennes prises par l’Algérie en juillet 2025 pour réduire et renforcer le contrôle sur ses importations avec l’instauration du Programme prévisionnel d’importation (PPI). Selon les chiffres officiels consultés par TSA, les exportations françaises vers l’Algérie se sont établies à 4 milliards d’euros durant les 12 derniers mois (juillet 2025-juin 2026) contre 4,9 milliards d’exportations algériennes vers l’Hexagone durant la même période. Commerce Algérie – France : l’agroalimentaire et l’automobile français en forte baisse En 2025, la France a exporté pour 4,2 milliards d’euros vers l’Algérie et en a importé 5,1 milliards, ce qui a induit un déficit commercial de 865 millions d’euros, le même que durant l’année 2025. Dans le détail, c’est l’agroalimentaire français qui a subi la plus forte baisse en glissement annuel (-60 %). Les exportations françaises vers l’Algérie sont passées de 119 millions d’euros durant la période de juillet 2024 à juin 2025 à 47 millions d’euros pendant la période de juillet 2025 à juin 2026. La deuxième forte baisse des exportations françaises vers l’Algérie concerne les équipements automobiles qui ont dégringolé de 37 %, passant de 102 millions d’euros à 64 millions d’euros. Les produits de la construction automobile, qui représentent 25 % des exportations françaises vers l’Algérie, ont également subi une baisse conséquente de 15 %, passant de 1,2 milliard d’euros à un milliard d’euros durant la période de référence. La troisième plus forte baisse des importations algériennes de France concerne les appareils de mesure, d’essais et de navigation ainsi que les articles d’horlogerie qui ont reculé de 36,6 % entre juillet 2024 et juin 2026, par rapport à la période juillet 2024 – juin 2025. Les produits sidérurgiques et de transformation d’acier français ont également reculé de 36,4 % pour s’établir à 94,6 millions d’euros. Hydrocarbures : les exportations algériennes vers la France en forte baisse Pour l’Algérie, ses exportations d’hydrocarbures vers la France ont chuté de 22 % entre juillet 2025 et juin 2024 à 3,5 milliards d’euros, soit une perte d’un milliard d’euros par rapport à la période juillet 2024 – juin 2025. Les importations françaises de produits pétroliers raffinés algériens ont légèrement baissé de 6,7 %, passant de 881,8 millions d’euros à 823 millions d’euros, en glissement annuel. Les hydrocarbures naturels ont représenté 72 % des exportations algériennes vers la France de juillet 2025 à juin 2026, contre 16,9 % pour les produits pétroliers raffinés et coke. Les produits hors hydrocarbures ne représentent que 3,3 % de l’ensemble des exportations algériennes vers la France. L’article Algérie – France : le commerce bilatéral dégringole sous les 9 milliards € est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: SOUM/Lancement du Tournoi Maracana de l’Espoir à Aribinda : Un succès pour la cohésion sociale
items.description: SOUM/Lancement du Tournoi Maracana de l'Espoir à Aribinda : Un succès pour la cohésion sociale Arbinda, 05 août 2026 (AIB)-Le Président de la Délégation Spéciale le Camarade Lazard KIEME a donné le coup d'envoi des activités du tant attendu tournoi Maracana « Tournoi de l'Espoir » dans la commune d'Aribinda. La journée a débuté sous les meilleurs auspices avec l'organisation d'un cross populaire, rassemblant la population dans un élan de fraternité et de sportivité. En milieu d'après-midi, à 16h00 précises, le terrain départemental d'Aribinda a vibré au rythme du match d'ouverture. La cérémonie s'est déroulée en présence de personnalités de marque, dont le représentant du parrain, le commandant du 28e Bataillon d'Intervention rapide (BIR), le président de la délégation spéciale d'Aribinda, ainsi que les autorités administratives, coutumières et les anciens de la commune. Le match inaugural a opposé deux équipes redoutables : le BIR 28 A et l'équipe des Volontaires pour la Défense de la Patrie (VDP). Au terme d'une rencontre disputée, c'est l'équipe du BIR 28 A qui a triomphé, s'imposant par un score de deux buts à zéro. Au-delà de la compétition sportive, ce tournoi se veut avant tout un vecteur de cohésion sociale. Il vise à renforcer les liens entre les différentes composantes de la société, à promouvoir le vivre-ensemble et à offrir un espace de détente et de partage aux habitants d'Aribinda. Les organisateurs espèrent que cette initiative contribuera durablement à la paix et à l'unité au sein de la communauté. Agence d'information du Burkina

items.title: Champions League 2026/27: draw date, qualified teams, final venue
items.description: The draw for the 2026/27 UEFA Champions League league phase is fast approaching, with Paris Saint-Germain set to begin their title defence as they chase an unprecedented third successive crown. Luis Enrique’s side successfully defended their crown last season, beating Arsenal on penalties in the final in Budapest after previously dismantling Inter Milan 5-0 in the 2025 final. PSG are now among 36 clubs chasing European football’s biggest prize, with qualifying already underway ahead of the start of the league phase in September. Here is everything to know about the 2026/27 Champions League league phase draw, participating clubs, schedule and final. When is the Champions League 2026/27 league phase draw? The draw for the 2026/27 Champions League league phase is scheduled for Thursday, August 27, 2026. It will begin at 5pm BST (12pm ET, 9am PT and 6pm CEST) and will take place at UEFA’s headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland. The draw is expected to be streamed through UEFA’s official digital platforms. Which teams have qualified for the 2026/27 Champions League? A majority of the 36 league-phase places have already been confirmed following the conclusion of domestic competitions across Europe. The remaining six places will be decided through the Champions League qualifying play-offs in August. England leads the way with six clubs in the league phase, while Spain has five representatives. Germany, Italy and France have four clubs each. Manchester United are back in the competition, while Aston Villa return after winning the Europa League. Roma, Real Betis, Lille and Shakhtar Donetsk are also returning after missing out in recent seasons. Italian side Como, meanwhile, are preparing for their first-ever appearance in the Champions League. Confirmed Champions League 2026/27 league-phase teams England Liverpool Arsenal Manchester City Chelsea Manchester United Aston Villa Spain Barcelona Real Madrid Atlético Madrid Real Betis Villarreal Germany Bayern Munich RB Leipzig Stuttgart Borussia Dortmund Italy Napoli Inter Milan Roma Como France Paris Saint-Germain Lens Lille Netherlands PSV Eindhoven Feyenoord Portugal Sporting CP Porto Türkiye Galatasaray Czechia Slavia Prague Belgium Club Brugge Ukraine Shakhtar Donetsk How will the Champions League league phase work? The Champions League continues to use its expanded 36-team league-phase format. Every club will play eight matches during the league phase, facing two teams from each of the four seeding pots. Each club will play four matches at home and four away. Once the eight rounds of fixtures are completed, the top eight teams in the table will qualify automatically for the last 16. Teams finishing between ninth and 24th will enter a two-legged knockout play-off, with the winners advancing to the round of 16. The teams finishing from 25th to 36th will be eliminated from the competition. From the play-off round onwards, the tournament will follow the traditional knockout format. When does the 2026/27 Champions League league phase start? The league phase is scheduled to begin on September 8, 2026, with Matchday 1 running until September 10. The competition will then continue through eight matchdays before the league phase concludes in January 2027. The scheduled dates are: The fixture schedule includes an extended gap between the opening two matchdays because of the international calendar. Where will the 2027 Champions League final be played? The Estadio Metropolitano in Madrid, Spain, will host the 2027 Champions League final. The stadium will stage the showpiece for the second time after previously hosting the 2019 final between Liverpool and Tottenham Hotspur. Liverpool won that all-English final 2-0 to claim their sixth European Cup. The 2027 final is scheduled for June 5, 2027, when the next European champions will be crowned. items.title: Liverpool set to sign Barcelona captain Araújo on loan
items.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Liverpool are reportedly close to completing a season-long loan deal for Barcelona captain Ronald Araújo, with the agreement also expected to include an option for a permanent transfer. According to veteran sports journalist Fabrizio Romano, sources familiar with the negotiations said the Uruguay international has accepted Liverpool’s proposal as he looks for more regular playing time away from Barcelona. The move would see Araújo join new Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola as the Premier League club seeks to strengthen its defensive options ahead of the new season. Araújo, 27, is primarily a centre-back but can also play at right-back, a versatility that could prove valuable to Liverpool, particularly with Conor Bradley currently sidelined through injury. Liverpool’s need for defensive reinforcements became increasingly evident during their pre-season tour of the United States. The club is also adjusting to the departure of Ibrahima Konaté, who left on a free transfer for Real Madrid at the end of last season. Araújo has made 213 first-team appearances for Barcelona since joining the club from Uruguayan side Boston River in 2018. He was promoted to the senior team in 2020 and eventually established himself as a key member of the defence and one of the club’s captains. However, his prominence in the squad has declined under manager Hansi Flick, with injuries also affecting his opportunities. Barcelona currently have several options in central defence, including Pau Cubarsí, Eric García, Gerard Martín and Andreas Christensen, further complicating Araújo’s chances of securing consistent first-team football. The defender reportedly believes a move to Liverpool would provide him with the opportunity to play more regularly while testing himself in the Premier League. The proposed loan would initially keep Araújo at Anfield for one season, while the option to make the move permanent could give Liverpool a chance to secure his services on a longer-term basis. items.title: Captain martyred, 7 terrorists killed in intelligence-based operation in Hangu: ISPR
items.description: The military’s media affairs wing said on Saturday that a captain was martyred while seven terrorists were killed during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Hangu district. In a statement , Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said security forces conducted an IBO in Hangu on Friday following reports about the presence of terrorists belonging to Fitna al Khawarij — a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan. During the operation, troops effectively engaged the terrorists, it said. “In desperation, the khawarij took refuge inside a mosque, blatantly disregarding the sanctity of the place of worship. In ensuing fire exchange, seven khawarij belonging to Indian-sponsored Fitna al Khawarij were sent to hell,” it said. The statement went on to say that during the exchange of fire, 27-year-old Captain Hamza Akram, a resident of Punjab’s Narowal district who was “leading his troops from front and relentlessly pursuing” the terrorists, embraced martyrdom. “Weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the killed khawarij , who remained actively involved in numerous terrorist activities against the security forces and law enforcement agencies as well as killing of innocent civilians,” it said. ISPR said that a sanitisation operation was being conducted to eliminate any other Indian-sponsored terrorists in the area. President Asif Ali Zardari paid tribute to the martyred captain, saying, “The motherland pays its profound tribute to the great sacrifice of its brave son.” “The entire nation is indebted to the eternal sacrifices of these brave sons for the motherland,” the president added, offering prayers for the bereaved family. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed deep grief over Captain Akram’s martyrdom while hailing his courage and devotion, state-run APP reported. In a statement issued by his office, PM Shehbaz lauded the security forces for eliminating seven terrorists “operating under the Indian patronage”. “The nation will never forget the sacrifices of its brave sons,” the press release quoted him as saying. He prayed for the captain’s elevated ranks and for patience for his family. The prime minister reiterated that operations against Fitna al Khawarij would continue till complete elimination of terrorism. “The sacrifices rendered by our brave armed forces and law-enforcement agencies for the defence, peace and security of the country and nation will not go in vain,” he asserted. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also paid tribute to the martyred captain and offered his condolences to the bereaved family. He said that the officer had paid the ultimate sacrifice for the homeland and would remain alive in our hearts. A day earlier, ISPR said 10 terrorists were killed in two separate engagements in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It said that in the first encounter, a group of terrorists attempted to attack security forces’ checkposts in Azam Warsak area in South Waziristan, which was effectively thwarted, resulting in the deaths of eight terrorists. “In another encounter that took place in Dir district, own troops successfully neutralised two more khawarij ,” it added. Terrorist commander killed in Bannu Separately, security forces killed a key terrorist commander, identified as Jamidullah, during an operation in Jani Khel area of KP’s Bannu district, a security official said. The official said that the terrorist commander was involved in terrorist activities and was considered a quadcopter expert. The official said that security forces conducted the operation in Jani Khel on the basis of intelligence reports, during which Jamidullah was targeted and killed. According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies , an Islamabad-based think tank, violence linked to terrorist attacks and counter-terrorism operations intensified sharply in July, making it the deadliest month of 2026, with 112 security personnel among 205 people killed.

items.title: 5 phones made in China that can rival the iPhone 17
items.description: The smartphone market is no longer dominated by Apple and Samsung. Chinese manufacturers have produced a growing number of premium phones with powerful processors, advanced cameras, fast charging and high-end displays. For buyers considering the Apple iPhone 17, several Chinese smartphones offer compelling alternatives, particularly for those who want different designs, stronger charging speeds or more camera-focused hardware. Here are five Chinese phones worth considering if you are looking beyond the iPhone 17. 1. Xiaomi 17 Pro Xiaomi has established itself as one of China’s biggest smartphone brands, and its flagship models increasingly compete with Apple’s premium iPhones. The Xiaomi 17 Pro is aimed at users who want flagship performance without being locked into Apple’s ecosystem. Its appeal centres on high-end hardware, photography capabilities and a premium design. For smartphone buyers who prioritise camera versatility, fast charging and Android’s greater flexibility, Xiaomi’s flagship can be an attractive alternative to the iPhone 17. 2. Huawei Pura 80 Pro Huawei continues to develop high-end smartphones despite the challenges it faces in international markets. The Huawei Pura 80 Pro is particularly interesting for photography enthusiasts. Huawei’s Pura series has become known for its emphasis on mobile photography, with sophisticated camera hardware and image-processing technology. It is therefore an option for buyers who place camera performance high on their list and want something different from Apple’s approach to smartphone photography. 3. OPPO Find X9 Pro Oppo has also become a major force in the premium smartphone market. The Find X9 Pro targets users looking for a high-end Android experience, combining flagship hardware with a strong focus on photography, display quality and battery technology. One of OPPO’s biggest advantages over the iPhone is the charging experience offered by its flagship phones. For users who dislike waiting around for a phone to recharge, this can be an important consideration. 4. vivo X300 Pro Vivo has built a reputation for producing smartphones with strong camera systems, particularly among users interested in portrait and telephoto photography. The vivo X300 Pro is designed as a premium flagship, with photography playing a major part in its appeal. Its combination of camera hardware, processing capabilities and Android flexibility makes it an interesting alternative for someone considering the iPhone 17 but wanting a more photography-focused Android phone. 5. OnePlus 13 OnePlus has traditionally focused on delivering flagship-level performance at prices that can undercut some of the industry’s biggest premium brands. The OnePlus 13 combines powerful hardware with a large high-resolution display, a capable camera system and fast charging. For consumers who care more about performance, battery life and charging than Apple’s ecosystem, OnePlus provides a strong alternative to the iPhone 17. items.title: UNIWIZ Foundation trains Greater Accra ICT coordinators in advanced digital skills
items.description: ICT coordinators from districts across the Greater Accra Region have undergone a two-day Advanced Digital Skills Training programme aimed at strengthening digital literacy and enhancing the delivery of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) education in schools. The training, which opened on Thursday, August 6, and ended on Friday August 7, at Methodist University, Dansoman, brought together ICT coordinators from across the region and selected ICT teachers from senior high schools to build their technical capacity through practical digital tools and strategies for teaching and learning. Organised by the UNIWIZ Foundation in partnership with the Ghana Education Service (GES), ModePlus Innovation Hub and Intellite IT Solutions, with support from the Embassy of Switzerland in Ghana, the training was held on the theme, “Advancing Ghana’s Education Technology Workforce.” Speaking at the opening ceremony, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of the UNIWIZ Foundation, Wisdom Larry Quarme-Doe, said although digital infrastructure is essential, it is educators who ultimately drive digital transformation in schools. “Digital infrastructure and computers alone do not transform our children. People do. The true drivers of digital literacy in our schools are our ICT coordinators. You are the digital champions guiding the next generation into the global economy.” He said the two-day programme was designed to equip participants with practical knowledge and advanced digital tools that would improve the integration of technology into teaching and learning. “This two-day intensive training is designed to equip you with advanced tools, practical skills and practical strategies to elevate educational technology across Ghana.” Mr Quarme-Doe urged participants to maximise the opportunity by learning from one another and embracing emerging technologies. “Over the next two days, immerse yourselves, exchange ideas, challenge your limits and embrace new technologies. The knowledge you take back to your respective institutions will cascade directly to thousands of young Ghanaians.” Representing the Greater Accra Regional Director of Education, Regional Planning Officer Ahmed Alhassan described the programme as timely, noting that ICT continues to play an increasingly significant role in Ghana’s education system. “ICT has now become a core subject at the basic level and it is now an elective at the WASSCE level. That is why I think this training is so important because those who are providing education for these kids need to have advanced skills in ICT so that they can also impact the children.” He said continuous capacity-building for ICT coordinators and teachers is necessary to ensure they remain equipped to teach evolving digital skills. “We need to always organise workshops for them to upgrade their knowledge and skills in ICT so that, at the end of it, it is the Ghanaian child who is in school that will be the biggest beneficiary of the programme.” Mr Alhassan observed that ICT education has improved over the years with the establishment of computer laboratories in many schools, although more infrastructure is still needed. “Previously, when ICT was introduced as an examinable subject at the basic level, because of lack of equipment and ICT materials, teaching it was very difficult. You cannot teach ICT in an abstract.” He therefore called on organisations and development partners to support efforts to expand ICT facilities across schools. “The issue is still about establishing more ICT labs in the schools. Government cannot do it all. Stakeholders who are willing to support the Ghanaian education system can come to our offices, and we can direct them to where we need these ICT labs, especially where we have clusters of schools.” According to the Embassy of Switzerland in Ghana they supported the training because it addresses the need to equip children with the digital skills required to thrive in today’s world. “The embassy is pleased to support this programme because it addresses some of the most important questions in our education sector today, information technology and how we ensure that children are equipped and ready for the world that they are in today.” They reminded participants that the knowledge gained should ultimately benefit learners. “All of us gathered here are not the final recipients of this programme. I want to urge you to at all times keep in mind the children who are indeed the ultimate beneficiaries of such a training.” Highlighting the pace of technological advancement globally, the representative from the Embassy said Ghanaian children must be supported to remain competitive. “We see them as athletes on the field, whereas ours are just about preparing in the dressing room to get on that track. That is how unfortunate the current situation is.” The two-day training combined presentations with practical sessions designed to strengthen participants’ digital competencies and enhance the teaching of ICT across schools in the Greater Accra Region.

items.title: From ‘Global Textile City’ to study tours in Benin Republic: The shame of Nigeria
items.description: Douglas Baye-Osagie It is sobering to see the Vice President of Nigeria lead a team of Governors to the Benin Republic to study the operations of a textile mill. Vice President Shettima flew into Cotonou, and pictures from his official verified Facebook page, Kashim Shettima, on 24th July 2026 carried a sentence: “drawing practical lessons from Benin’s approach to agricultural value chain.” The images tell a story we should not be telling in 2026. Not long ago, the story was reversed. People came to Nigeria. Buyers came. Investors came. Technicians came. They came to learn how we did it. The textile industry provided millions of jobs for Nigerians across different classes. There was a time in the 70s, 80s and 90s when the world came to Nigeria for textiles. Our mills ran 24 hours. Our markets were full of “Made in Nigeria” fabrics. We had functional textile mills across the country. That was not a projection. That was reality. Spindles turned. Looms moved. Paychecks were issued every month. At its peak, the industry was the largest employer of labour after government. It provided jobs for hundreds of thousands of Nigerians directly. It also supported hundreds of thousands of cotton farmers across many states. From the farm, to the ginnery, to the mill, to the tailor, to the market. One value chain. Millions of livelihoods. Kaduna was then called the “Textile City” of Africa. If you lived there, you could hear the hum of machines in the morning. Entire neighbourhoods grew around the factories. The convergence of Nigerians in Kaduna was largely because of the booming cotton factories. Young men left their states to seek a start to life. Great men like Sen. Adams Oshiomhole began their humble rise in the textile industry back then in Kaduna State. He was a factory worker before he became a union leader, then Governor, then Senator. That ladder existed because the factories existed. Writing for the Daily Trust Newspaper on 7 April 2026, Hassan Hussain wrote: “But the textile industry was never solely a Northern phenomenon. Chief Obafemi Awolowo established textile industries in the West, including Western Nigeria Textile Mills in Ikeja, drawing on cotton grown by Yoruba farmers in Abeokuta—cotton with the highest staple length and finest fibres among Nigerian varieties. Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe pursued industrial development with equal vigour, establishing textile mills in Aba and other eastern cities, drawing on northern cotton and local cultivation. By the 1970s, Nigeria had achieved what few African nations could boast: a truly national textile industry.” Read about Arewa Textiles. Read about United Nigerian Textiles. Read about Aba Textiles, Supertex, Nortex, Finetex, Gaskiya, Alprint. These were not just company names. They were institutions. They trained engineers. They funded schools. They sponsored football clubs. They built cities. Across the country, the textile trade was booming. Kano, Lagos, Aba, Funtua, Asaba, Benin. Every region had a hub. Nigeria was one of the largest textile producers in Africa. So what happened? The decline did not happen in one day. It was death by a thousand cuts. First, we abandoned cotton. The oil boom made us lazy. We stopped prioritizing agriculture, and cotton production collapsed. Then came trade liberalisation under WTO agreements without safeguards. Our markets were flooded with cheap imports and smuggled fabrics. Local goods could not compete. The Structural Adjustment Program removed subsidies and protections that the mills needed to survive. Electricity became unreliable. Interest rates went up. Later, massive imports finished what policy failures had started. The number of operating mills dropped drastically. Today, only a handful remain and employment in the sector is a shadow of what it used to be. Then finally came insecurity and banditry, which drove farmers away from their farms. The Vice President may be genuinely concerned about learning from the Benin Republic, but we must fix our problems at home first before going to Cotonou. And that is why the current posture hurts. We can’t put politics above governance and expect development. Governance is about systems, not slogans. We keep appointing lobbyists, poorly educated career politicians instead of professionals to head technical positions. We reward none over knowledge. We put people who “know people” in charge of things that require people who “know the work.” The result is what we see: the gradual collapse of critical sectors of the economy. When the local institutions fail, the whole country goes to the Benin Republic to take notes. We must look inwards before it is too late. Reviving textiles is not about motions in the Senate. It is about funding industry banks, protecting local production, reviving cotton, fixing power, and putting professionals in charge. The blueprint is in our history. The “Textile City” is still in Kaduna. We just have to decide to turn the machines on again. dbayosagie@yahoo.com Vanguard News The post From ‘Global Textile City’ to study tours in Benin Republic: The shame of Nigeria appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: DSS arrests three more suspects linked to Nasarawa varsity professor’s kidnap
items.description: By Soni Daniel Operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS) on Friday night arrested three more persons suspected to be members of the group linked to the abduction of the Dean of Agriculture at Nasarawa State University, Professor Samuel Avengbe Okunsebor. The university don was rescued by DSS operatives two days after he was abducted by gunmen in the early hours of Wednesday, July 15, 2026, at Mile Uku, a border community between Lafia and Nasarawa-Eggon Local Government Areas. Two suspects, including a woman, were arrested by the DSS at the time. A security source disclosed that the three other suspects were arrested on Friday night at a local brothel along the Mararaban Akunza-Lafia-Makurdi highway. According to the source, the suspects were identified as 25-year-old Yakubu Abubakar, also known as Black/Starboy, from the Doemak community in Plateau State; 37-year-old Usman Abubakar Mairiga; and 27-year-old Sale Babauro Abubakar. The source said Mairiga and Sale Babauro Abubakar are of Hausa and Fulani backgrounds respectively. The source further disclosed that the suspects were being held at the State Command for further investigation, following a valid detention warrant obtained from a magistrate’s court. items.title: Every Journey a Gamble: Life on Benin-Warri Road of pains
items.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi By the time dawn breaks over Benin City, motorists heading for Warri have already accepted one certainty: no one knows when the journey will end. Read Also: 2 25 children from Kebbi, Kwara, Niger died in terrorists’ captivity — Lawmaker What should take barely an hour often stretches into six, eight or even an entire day. Articulated trucks sink into craters that swallow their tyres, commercial buses weave dangerously between failed sections. Traders watch perishable goods rot in traffic, while stranded commuters keep one eye on the road and another on the surrounding bushes, fearful of kidnappers and armed robbers. For thousands who depend on the Benin-Sapele-Warri Road, every trip is no longer routine. It is a gamble with time, livelihood and, sometimes, life itself. Across the Niger Delta, abandoned federal highways have long symbolised unfulfilled promises. For years, the East-West Road stood as the region’s most visible reminder of delayed contracts, cost variations and shifting contractors. Today, many commuters believe the Benin-Sapele-Warri Road has overtaken it as the most painful symbol of that neglect. The perception gained fresh momentum after the Federal Government approved N1.9 trillion for 27 road projects across 15 states, with no major federal road projects announced for Delta, Edo, Bayelsa, Rivers or Akwa Ibom States. To many residents, the omission reinforced a long-standing feeling that the region’s infrastructure deficit continues to receive inadequate attention. For Victor Okpamos, former Chairman, Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Warri Correspondents’ Chapel, the statistics are secondary to the daily suffering he witnesses on the Oghara-Mosogar axis. Nearly two weeks after Delta State announced emergency intervention on the failed section, he said the promised relief had yet to materialise. “Governor Sheriff Oborevwori, please kindly prevail on Obekpor Engineering Company to commence work in the interest of the people to ease suffering of motorists and other road users. Some stationeries are on-site, no equipment, no manpower. The people are waiting and suffering in silence. The situation is agonising”, Okpamos appealed. His account goes beyond damaged vehicles: “Someone said a bike man raped his passenger, a married woman yesterday, and a motor boy was crushed by his trailer; he died on the spot. “President Bola Tinubu and David Umahi should wake up from their slumber and give the East-West Expressway a permanent repair.” Stories of fear, delay and economic hardship have become increasingly common along the corridors. Civil society leader Rev. David Ugolor believes the consequences extend far beyond transportation. Ugolor highlighted, “The continued deterioration undermines economic growth, threatens public safety and weakens national development. ‘Lives have been lost in avoidable road accidents. Businesses have suffered severe economic losses. Farmers struggle to move their produce. Patients are delayed from accessing healthcare.” According to him, worsening road conditions have also fuelled insecurity: “More alarming is the growing insecurity. The deplorable condition of the road has created opportunities for kidnappers and other criminal elements who prey on stranded motorists and commuters.” While commending Governor Sheriff Oborevwori for ordering emergency repairs, Ugolor warned against what he described as the endless cycle of temporary interventions. “Without comprehensive reconstruction, many of these repaired sections may deteriorate again within a short period, resulting in another cycle of emergency interventions funded by taxpayers. This is neither economically prudent nor sustainable,” he stated. The debate over the road has also exposed widening political fault lines. Social justice advocate Zik Gbemre argues that while communities elsewhere in the Niger Delta have successfully mobilised political leaders to demand federal intervention, Delta has lacked the same unified voice. “Today every stakeholder in Delta is singing, ‘On your mandate we stand,’ even while the President’s neglect of the Benin-Sapele Road has assumed inciting proportion, with transporters and commuters suffering untold hardship that escalates as the rains peak”, is what he said. He contrasted the situation with collective agitations over the Itu-Calabar Road and the Eleme-Onne Section of the East-West Road, where sustained pressure from lawmakers, traditional rulers and host communities eventually prompted renewed federal attention. The growing frustration eventually reached the Senate floor. Senator Adams Oshiomhole openly challenged the Federal Ministry of Works over what he described as an imbalance in road development affecting Edo and Delta States. “Three weeks ago I understand 20 new roads were approved. But between Edo and Delta, there is manifest bias by the Minister of Works. You’re here, Senator Dahiru. You can’t go to Warri from Benin, can’t go to Asaba from Benin, can’t go to Auchi from Benin, can’t go to Okene from Benin. What have we done wrong?” Works Minister David Umahi rejected the criticism, arguing that the Benin-Warri Road contract had been awarded in 2018 and suggesting previous administrations also bore responsibility for delays. Yet concerns about how federal roads in the Niger Delta are managed predate the current administration. Following a fact-finding mission in 2023, the Senate Ad-hoc Committee on the East-West Road identified engineering compromises, contract duplication and deviations from approved designs as major contributors to repeated failures. Then Committee Chairman, Senator Abdul Ahmed Nimingi, expressed concern over what lawmakers found: “We saw from initial concept engineering that they did not do the scientific needful of testing the soil… and that has to do with some compromises. This is unacceptable.” These findings continue to resonate as motorists navigate another rainy season on the Benin-Sapele-Warri Road. Each failed section tells the story of contracts awarded but unfinished, emergency repairs that seldom outlast a season, and communities forced to adjust their lives around a highway that should have been a gateway to commerce and development. Until comprehensive reconstruction replaces recurring palliative repairs, commuters will continue to leave home with uncertainty rather than confidence. On the Benin-Warri Road, every kilometre tells a story. For too many in the Niger Delta, it is a story of neglect that has lasted far too long. The post Every Journey a Gamble: Life on Benin-Warri Road of pains appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: CAN féminine 2026 : le Maroc vise le dernier carré et un billet pour le Mondial 2027
items.description: Les Lionnes de l'Atlas ont rendez-vous avec leur histoire. Opposées à l'Afrique du Sud ce samedi (21h00) au stade Moulay El Hassan de Rabat, les Marocaines joueront bien plus qu'une qualification pour les demi-finales de la Coupe d'Afrique des nations féminine 2026. En cas de victoire, elles décrocheront également leur billet pour la Coupe du monde féminine 2027, prévue au Brésil. Premières du groupe A avec sept points, les joueuses de Jorge Vilda abordent ce quart de finale avec confiance après une phase de groupes réussie. Elles ont successivement dominé le Kenya (4-0), battu l'Algérie (1-0), avant de partager les points avec le Sénégal (0-0). L'un des principaux atouts des Lionnes réside dans leur solidité défensive. Aucune équipe n'est parvenue à trouver le chemin des filets face aux Marocaines depuis le début du tournoi, preuve de l'équilibre et de la discipline tactique du groupe. Emmenées par des joueuses d'expérience comme Ghizlane Chebbak, Ibtissam Jraïdi et Sanaa Mssoudy, les Marocaines devront toutefois se montrer plus efficaces offensivement face aux Banyana Banyana, championnes d'Afrique en titre. L'Afrique du Sud a connu un parcours plus difficile lors de la phase de groupes. Battues d'entrée par la Tanzanie (2-1), les Sud-Africaines ont ensuite concédé un nul face à la Côte d'Ivoire (2-2) avant de valider leur qualification grâce à une victoire contre le Burkina Faso (1-0), terminant deuxièmes du groupe B avec quatre points. Cette rencontre aura également une saveur particulière pour les Lionnes de l'Atlas. Elles retrouveront l'équipe qui les avait privées d'un premier sacre continental lors de la finale de la CAN 2022, remportée par les Sud-Africaines sur le score de 2-1. Portées par leur public, les Marocaines auront ainsi l'occasion de prendre leur revanche tout en poursuivant leur rêve de décrocher un premier titre continental. Au-delà d'une place dans le dernier carré, ce quart de finale offre un enjeu majeur : une qualification directe pour la Coupe du monde féminine 2027 au Brésil, un objectif qui permettrait au football féminin marocain de confirmer sa progression sur la scène internationale. The post CAN féminine 2026 : le Maroc vise le dernier carré et un billet pour le Mondial 2027 appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Osun Decides: Election is not warfare, stop militarising it — Accord tells FG
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike The Accord Party, on Friday, demanded the immediate resignation of the Chairman of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, accusing the anti-graft agency of partisanship and interference in the August 15 governorship election in Osun State. Read Also: Osun Decides: I’ll block leakages, expand revenue – Oyebamiji The party said the demand followed the EFCC’s now-reversed freezing of the Osun State Government’s bank account, which it described as the latest in a series of actions that had heightened fears of institutional interference in the state’s electoral process. Speaking at a world press conference in Abuja, Accord National Chairman, Chief Maxwell Mgbudem, said the party had lost confidence in the EFCC leadership and called on President Bola Tinubu to sack its chairman if he failed to resign. “Having demonstrated unprecedented partisanship in the Osun State politics, assaulted the sensibilities of fellow compatriots and brought the nation to ridicule and disrepute before the international community, Accord has lost confidence in the current leadership of the EFCC,” Mgbudem said. He accused the commission of exceeding its statutory mandate by freezing the state government’s account on August 5, saying the action threatened public confidence in democratic institutions. “Accordingly, Accord demands the immediate resignation of the EFCC chairman. For embarrassing the President, the Party, the Government and people of Osun State and fellow citizens. The EFCC chairman should toe the path of honour and tender his resignation. If he fails to resign, President Tinubu should sack him immediately to restore the integrity of the anti-graft agency,” the Accord chairman stated. The party chairman said the EFCC action came against the backdrop of what Accord described as months of political violence and intimidation in Osun, with members and supporters allegedly killed, shot, arrested, harassed and intimidated. Mgbudem also alleged that the offices of the Imole Campaign Council and the party in the state had been attacked, while campaign billboards were destroyed by suspected thugs linked to the All Progressives Congress, APC. According to him, Accord had reported the alleged attacks to security agencies and, in some cases, notified them ahead of planned incidents, but accused the authorities of failing to prevent the attacks or arrest those responsible. He said the party had initially welcomed the decision by the Inspector-General of Police to deploy a new Commissioner of Police to Osun following public concern over the security situation, but alleged that the EFCC’s intervention had subsequently aggravated the political atmosphere. Mgbudem said the development reinforced the party’s fears of an attempt to use federal institutions to weaken Governor Ademola Adeleke’s administration ahead of the election. “EFCC joined the Osun political fray hoping to succeed where the earlier compromised State Police Command failed by deliberately turning the law upside down to justify its unconstitutional action that threatened the foundations of the country’s emerging democracy,” he alleged. But he commended Tinubu for intervening after the Osun State Government, Accord and other Nigerians appealed to him, saying the President’s order for the immediate reversal of the account freeze had helped avert further escalation. “Accord welcomes President Tinubu’s timely intervention in this critical national issue and urges security agencies, anti-graft commissions, electoral umpire and relevant democratic institutions to strictly abide by their rules of engagements, statutory duties and democratic ethics,” Mgbudem said. He, however, warned the Federal Government against deploying state institutions in a manner that could compromise the August 15 poll. “Electoral contest is not a warfare. It should not be militarized by deploying federal apparatuses to suppress, subdue and oppress political opponents and their supporters to favour a party that has been rejected by the people,” he warned. He said Osun residents must be allowed to freely choose their governor, insisting that Accord would not bow to intimidation. The party chairman described Osun as an Accord stronghold and said Adeleke deserved a second term, citing his administration’s performance and what he called its delivery of dividends of democracy. Mgbudem also alleged that there had been previous attempts to destabilise the state government, including a court action seeking the deregistration of Accord and four other political parties. “It was to abruptly stop Adeleke’s transformative leadership that an attempt was made by the so-called former legislators to use the court to de-register Accord, four other political parties were merely added to cover-up their hidden agenda,” he said. He further alleged that the paralysis of local government operations and withholding of federal allocations to the councils were part of efforts to weaken Adeleke’s administration. According to him, those efforts had failed and would not stop the electorate from deciding the governor’s fate at the ballot box. The party urged Osun voters to come out in large numbers on August 15, vote for Adeleke and protect their ballots, insisting that every vote must be counted and reflected in the final result. It also charged the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, to conduct a free, fair, credible and inclusive election, describing the poll as particularly important because it would be the last off-cycle governorship election before the 2027 general elections. Accord urged INEC to adequately test its electoral materials and systems ahead of the poll, warning that glitches or operational failures could worsen an already tense political environment. The party called on the international community, civil society organisations, election observer missions, the Nigerian Bar Association, NBA, the media, development partners, opposition political parties and other stakeholders to closely monitor the election and speak out against any conduct capable of undermining its credibility. It said the poll must be free from violence, intimidation, harassment, unlawful interference by security agencies, manipulation, voter suppression and vote-buying. Security agencies, Accord said, must remain professional and impartial, with their constitutional responsibility limited to protecting lives, maintaining law and order and providing a secure environment for voters. “The people of Osun State deserve nothing less than an election whose outcome genuinely reflects their freely expressed democratic choice,” the Accord chairman said. The party also appealed to Tinubu and the Inspector-General of Police to release what it described as the remaining 60 Accord members detained by the police in Abuja, Osun and Nasarawa states. Mgbudem said the release of the detainees would help reduce the political tension surrounding the election. He said Accord was fully prepared for the poll and expressed confidence that the party would emerge victorious on August 15. “Accord is ready and prepared for the governorship election and will emerge victorious having fulfilled its campaign promises to the people in spite of the activities of detractors to frustrate Adeleke’s government,” he declared. The post Osun Decides: Election is not warfare, stop militarising it — Accord tells FG appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kombissiri : Les imams et prêcheurs de la commune outillés pour la promotion des valeurs de paix et de cohésion sociale
items.description: Burkina-Bazèga-Religion Kombissiri : Les imams et prêcheurs de la commune outillés pour la promotion des valeurs de paix et de cohésion sociale Kombissiri, 07 juillet 2026 (AIB) Le CERFI, à travers le projet Djama Béog néré, organise les 7 et 8 août 2026 à Kombissiri une formation au profit des imams et prêcheurs de la commune. L'objectif est de promouvoir le vivre-ensemble et la cohésion sociale pour un Burkina Faso de paix. Le Burkina Faso fait face depuis quelques années à une crise sécuritaire qui met à mal le vivre-ensemble, la paix et le respect mutuel entre les différentes composantes du pays. Dans l'optique de faire face à cette situation, le Centre d'études, de recherches et de formation islamiques (CERFI) s'est engagé à jouer sa partition en mettant en œuvre son projet de renforcement de la résilience des populations à travers la promotion des valeurs de paix, de cohésion sociale, de vivre-ensemble et des droits humains, dénommé ‹‹Djama Béog néré››. Pour ce faire, le CERFI a initié une formation de quarante-huit heures à l'intention des imams et prêcheurs de la commune de Kombissiri, qui vont échanger sur diverses thématiques de promotion des valeurs de paix. Pour le camarade Dr Kadré Sawadogo, 1er vice-président du CERFI et coordonnateur du projet, l'atelier de formation à Kombissiri consistera à outiller les imams et les prédicateurs sur les thématiques de cohésion sociale, de culture de la paix, de lutte contre l'extrémisme violent, les discours haineux et la stigmatisation, à la lumière des préceptes de l'islam. Selon lui, les défis que connaît le Burkina Faso ne sont pas insurmontables, ‹‹si nous nous appuyons sur nos valeurs fondamentales, aussi bien traditionnelles que religieuses››, a-t-il précisé. La camarade haut-commissaire de la province du Bazèga, Téné Justine Kientega/Ilboudo, qui a présidé la cérémonie d'ouverture des travaux, a salué l'initiative du CERFI et le travail abattu au quotidien par les imams et prédicateurs en faveur de la paix au Burkina Faso. Elle a invité les participants à cette formation à s'approprier les différentes thématiques en vue de jouer pleinement le rôle qui est le leur dans un Burkina en quête de paix et de sécurité, débarrassé des stigmates des discours haineux et de violence. Selon le camarade Dr Kadré Sawadogo, le projet est mis en œuvre en partenariat avec l'Union des religieux et des coutumiers du Burkina pour la promotion de la santé et le développement (URCB/SD). Il est prévu pour s'étendre sur une durée de 32 mois et touchera 20 communes réparties dans 12 régions. Pour le coordonnateur, le travail s'effectue avec une approche inclusive et participative, et mobilise toutes les sensibilités islamiques présentes dans les régions et les localités concernées. Agence d'information du Burkina TPT/ata

items.title: Osun Decides: I’ll block leakages, expand revenue – Oyebamiji
items.description: By Clifford Ndujihe & Juliet Umeh The All Progressives Congress, APC, governorship candidate in the August 15 Osun State election, Asiwaju Munirudeen Bola Oyebamiji, AMBO, in this interview speaks on his chances, allegations of political violence, his plans to stabilise the state’s finances, expand revenue through technology, reduce government spending, implement local government autonomy, and deliver on his administration’s prosperity agenda, if elected. On why he is running I am a credible alternative to the current administration in Osun State. I served as the Commissioner for Finance under the administrations of Governors Rauf Aregbesola and Adegboyega Oyetola. Before then, I served as the Managing Director of the Osun Investment Company Limited, now known as Omoluabi Holdings Limited. To properly situate why Osun deserves a better deal at this time, the last allocation received by the APC administration of Governor Gboyega Oyetola from the Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) stood at approximately N2.6 billion. Today, the average monthly allocation to the state is about ¦ 16 billion without commensurate values to the state and her citizens. In fact, few of the infrastructure projects delivered by the current administration were awarded in secrecy to incompetent contractors while many of such projects have failed before commissioning. I am contesting to arrest the current drift in the state. Our Prosperity Agenda has continued to gain widespread acceptance among the people of Osun. So far, we have taken our campaign to all the 30 local government areas of the state. As a party, our firm belief is that the primary responsibility of any government, as provided in the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, is the security and welfare of its citizens. Consequently, our Prosperity Agenda is built on seven key pillars: P – Poverty Alleviation, Workers’ Welfare, and Job Creation; R – Responsive, Accountable, and Transparent Governance; O – Opportunities for Economic Growth, Support Programmes for Small and Medium-Scale Enterprises (SMEs), and Youth and Women Empowerment; S – Security, Safety, and Social Protection; P – Productive Agriculture Through Public-Private Partnerships and Rural Development; E – Education, Skills Development, and Targeted Investment in Healthcare Delivery; and R – Renewed Investment in Infrastructure to Drive Inclusive Growth, Culture, and Tourism. In line with our campaign promises, within our first 100 days in office, we will undertake a comprehensive review of all outstanding entitlements owed to active and retired workers and commence immediate payment. We are equally committed to ensuring that the Dagbolu Dry Port becomes fully operational. In addition to these, through strategic partnerships, we will commence the training and empowerment of not fewer than 10,000 young people in information and communication technology. We will also institutionalise monthly meetings of the State Security Council involving security agencies, traditional rulers, and local government leaders. Furthermore, we will launch pilot off-grid renewable energy projects in selected public institutions and rural communities. Similarly, we will conduct a comprehensive fiscal sustainability review covering state revenue, expenditure, and debt obligations. We will also undertake a state-wide infrastructure audit to identify priority economic roads and other critical infrastructure needs. These, among others, are the initiatives that we consider essential within our first one hundred days in office. We want to reassure Osun people and Nigerians that both the APC and I have been victims of the persistent political violence in Osun State. During the 2022 governorship election, more than 25 members of our party were allegedly murdered by members of the political party in power in Osun. In my own local government area for example, the Chairman of Irewole Local Government, Remi Abass, was killed within the council secretariat. Our party has also documented several other politically-motivated attacks and killings, for which we continue to seek justice through the courts. The ongoing political violence in the state has all the signs of the government in power on it. Just recently, the Inspector-General of Police visited Osun State and publicly raised allegations concerning individuals accused of criminal activities being housed within the Government House. Reports also emerged a few days ago concerning the arrest of a suspected criminal within the private residence of the Secretary to the State Government in Osogbo. Furthermore, reports on Sunday night indicated that some of our members were attacked in Ede, the hometown of Governor Ademola Adeleke. As an opposition party, these are some of the experiences of members of our party. Ironically, it is the Accord party and the government of Adeleke that would cry foul while our members bear the scars of political violence. What are the conditions that will guarantee a free and fair governorship election in Osun State? For us, first of all, we are going to abide by the rule of law, especially relying on INEC rules and security rules. If I have to take you back to the memory lane, the antecedents of APC in this country is not about violence. Violence is synonymous to the opposition. Especially if you look at all the states that APC has governors, there has not been any violence propelled, driven, or initiated by the APC government. It is not in our character and it is the same in Osun. About three-four months ago, we wrote to the IG, the policy commissioner, the director of DSS and the Commander of Civil Defence Corp, the opposition had designed, customised vehicles in APC colours and used those vehicles to perpetuate criminal activities. We are privileged to have that information and we inform them accordingly. All those criminal activities that have been perpetrated in Osun are being initiated by the Accord party. And we have written to the INEC and the security operators. It is important for them to take that into account. On his chances of winning the election Politics is about numbers. This time around, we have the numbers on our side. On how he would get funds to execute his prosperity agenda We have done it in the past during the Rauf Areghesola regime when I was the Commissioner for Finance. I came in May, by July, I had stabilised the finance of the state. The first thing is to block the leakages and cut the cost of governance. We won’t witch-hunt anyone The second one is to expand the revenue base. We have done it in the past. During Oyetola’s regime, the World Bank gave an award to the state as the best managed and profitable revenue enhancement state. We will deploy efficient technology to expand the finance base of the Osun State. On his plan for local government autonomy The Supreme Court has ruled, local government autonomy is here to stay. Even before the autonomy of the local government, during Oyetola’s tenure, we had never been involved in the activities of the local government. Is the zoning formula in Osun State in your favour? On zoning, what we have in Osun is one APC, and the current governor is from the West, I’m also from the West. So, I can confidently say that come 15th of August, I will win that election. On his assessment of Governor Ademola Adeleke’s performance Our position is that the current administration has not justified the enormous resources at its disposal. This assessment is based on publicly available information regarding federal allocations, intervention funds, and other revenues received by the state. The critical question is whether those resources have translated into visible improvements in the lives of ordinary people. When governments receive substantial revenues, citizens expect corresponding progress in education, healthcare, infrastructure, agriculture, employment and economic development. We believe there are legitimate questions regarding priorities, project implementation and overall outcomes. Have schools improved sufficiently? Has healthcare become more accessible? Have roads and other public infrastructure been upgraded? Have enough jobs been created? These are not partisan questions. Every citizen has the right to demand accountability because public resources belong to the people. Our campaign is centred on measurable performance, responsible governance and a clear vision for the future of Osun State. You have criticised some infrastructure projects undertaken by the government. What are your concerns? Our concerns centre on value for money, transparency and quality of execution. Infrastructure is important, but citizens deserve assurance that public funds are being spent responsibly. Whenever huge sums are committed to projects, the government should be transparent about costs, procurement processes, implementation timelines and expected outcomes. We have also raised concerns about aspects of some road and bridge projects, including questions about construction standards and project delivery. Infrastructure should be built to last and should serve communities for generations. Our criticism is not opposition for its own sake. We simply believe every naira spent should produce measurable value for the people. If elected, transparency, accountability and value for money will guide every infrastructure project undertaken by our administration. What distinguishes your campaign from that of your opponents? Our campaign is distinguished by its focus on governance and practical solutions. We are not interested in propaganda or personal attacks. Our emphasis is on issues that affect ordinary citizens every day, job creation, infrastructure, education, healthcare, agriculture and economic development. We believe politics should be about offering solutions rather than trading insults. That is the approach we have adopted, and it is the approach we intend to sustain if elected. His take on political violence in Osun State Political violence remains a serious concern, and it should worry every stakeholder regardless of political affiliation. Democracy thrives only when citizens can freely express their opinions, participate in political activities and vote without fear. Our party has repeatedly raised concerns over attacks on some of our members and supporters. Over the years, APC members have reportedly been attacked, injured, and, in some cases, killed. We have consistently brought these incidents to the attention of security agencies because every allegation of violence deserves proper investigation. In 2022 alone, we lost 25 members to political violence. That is now history, but it is a painful reminder that no political office is worth the life of any citizen. Political competition should never degenerate into violence. Regardless of political differences, we remain members of the same communities and citizens of the same state. I believe political leaders have a responsibility to promote peace. They must be careful with their words and actions because supporters often take their cue from them. We should encourage dialogue, tolerance and respect for differing opinions. The APC is not a violent party. Violence is not part of our political culture. We intend to win the confidence of voters through our ideas, performance and programmes rather than intimidation. Unfortunately, from what we have witnessed, those currently in government appear determined to deploy violence as a political tool. But your opponents argue that the APC is responsible for tension in the state. We reject that narrative completely. Elections should be decided on governance, policies and performance, not on allegations or hostility. We have, on several occasions, received intelligence about planned acts of violence and alerted the appropriate security agencies to what we believe the Accord Party intended to do. Whatever is happening in Osun today is being propelled by those in power. Our focus remains on presenting our programmes while allowing voters to make informed decisions. Democracy works best when citizens have clear choices based on facts and performance. The party in office is the one harbouring political thugs to attack us. You have made allegations regarding criminal activities and security issues in the state. Can you elaborate? Our position has always been that the rule of law must prevail. Where individuals are accused of criminal offences, investigations should be thorough, transparent and allowed to run their course without political interference. We have expressed concern over reports that some criminal cases were discontinued because such developments naturally raise public questions. Citizens deserve confidence that justice is being administered fairly. No one should be presumed guilty without due process, but serious allegations should never be ignored. Law enforcement agencies and the judiciary must remain independent and professional. Political considerations should never interfere with the administration of justice because public confidence depends on the integrity of these institutions. What message do you have for security agencies ahead of the election? My message is simple: remain professional, impartial and committed to the rule of law. Security agencies have a constitutional responsibility to protect every citizen regardless of political affiliation. Their duty is to maintain peace, prevent violence and ensure that voters can exercise their democratic rights without fear. Every reported case of violence or intimidation should be thoroughly investigated, and anyone found culpable should face the law. Accountability is essential to maintaining public confidence. We do not require federal might to win the Osun governorship election. We believe the people of Osun will freely choose the candidate they consider best prepared to govern the state. The post Osun Decides: I’ll block leakages, expand revenue – Oyebamiji appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Tinubu deserves praise for works across Nigeria – Onanuga
items.description: Presidential spokesperson Bayo Onanuga has said that President Bola Tinubu deserves praise for expanding infrastructure across the country. Onanuga stated this during an inspection tour of the Makurdi–Otukpo–Obolo-Affor–Enugu dual carriageway by the Renewed Hope Ambassadors Presidential Media Team. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the team led by Onanuga is being conducted round completed and ongoing federal and state infrastructure projects across Benue State. Speaking to newsmen along the corridor, Onanuga described the expressway as a landmark project that would strengthen connectivity, boost commerce and foster national integration. “From what we have seen so far, even though we have not even completed this road, it has shortened the travel time between Makurdi and Otukpo. “From what I gathered, the road was so bad that from Makurdi to Otukpo it used to take about three hours. But now, just about one and a half hours or so, we are in Otukpo. “So, this is a commendable project and I think President Bola Tinubu deserves a lot of applause for touching almost every part of Nigeria, giving them one road or bridge or one infrastructure or the other,” he said. Onanuga added: “This road is linking the North Central and the South East for you. “If you are able to link all parts of Nigeria, it shows you that we are improving the connectivity across our states. “This will no doubt boost, not just passenger traffic, also business as people will be able to move goods across all the borders, all the state borders”. Speaking on the project, the Federal Controller of Works, Benue State, Mukaila Danladi, said the 258-kilometre dual carriageway had been divided into five sections to facilitate construction. He explained that the project traverses Nasarawa, Benue, Kogi and Enugu states, forming a strategic transport corridor linking major economic and commercial centres across the regions. According to the controller, about 178 kilometres of the highway fall within Benue, while the section under inspection covers 50 kilometres on each carriageway, totalling 100 kilometres. Danladi said construction had progressed to about 86 kilometres of binder course on both carriageways, describing the achievement as significant in spite of prevailing weather-related challenges. He attributed the slower pace of work to the rainy season, noting that some earthworks could not be undertaken under unfavourable weather conditions common during construction. The controller, however, said work had not stopped, with contractors concentrating on hydraulic structures and drainage installations along the alignment pending improved weather conditions. He reiterated the Federal Government’s assurance that the project would be delivered within the 48-month contract period, with completion expected by December 2027. Danladi recalled that the highway is the second phase of the Abuja-Akwanga-Nasarawa-Makurdi corridor, extending the dualisation from Makurdi through Otukpo and Obollo-Afor to Enugu. He said the project is funded through a combination of the China EXIM Bank loan and Federal Government counterpart funding, while China Harbour Engineering Company is executing the works. NAN reports that the highway is expected to improve road safety, reduce travel time, ease movement of agricultural produce and strengthen trade and economic integration across the affected states. (NAN) The post Tinubu deserves praise for works across Nigeria – Onanuga appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Locafrique : Khadim Ba libéré

items.title: Osun account: Law mandates EFCC to serve court order – State counsel
items.description: Counsel to the Osun State Government, Prof. Mubarak Adekilekun (SAN), has argued that neither the state government nor First Bank was served with any court order accompanying the directive that restricted access to the state’s statutory allocation account. Adekilekun made the claim on Friday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today, while commenting on the controversy surrounding the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission’s action on the account. According to him, the law requires that a court order be obtained and properly served, particularly on the bank involved, before such a restriction can take effect. He explained that the EFCC initially wrote to First Bank, and the letter was later forwarded to the Osun State Government, but the bank indicated that no court order was attached to the correspondence. “You will recall that after the letter was written to First Bank in Osun, which in turn transmitted the letter to the state government, the requirement of the law in this regard is that a court order must be issued and served on, especially, First Bank. “The letter was forwarded to Osun State Government, where First Bank confirmed that no court order was attached to it,” Adekilekun said. The senior advocate acknowledged that the EFCC possesses statutory powers to act in cases involving suspected financial crimes, but maintained that those powers must be interpreted together with the provisions of the Money Laundering (Prevention and Prohibition) Act. “They were trying to justify their action that if they do not do it, the account could be compromised. Yes, we agree there are some provisions of the law that say EFCC can, but if you interpret this in conjunction with Section 7 of the MLA, it says that there must be a court order served on that party. “You can’t just go in and say, ‘Er, we are using our power vested in the Chairman of EFCC to now put a PND on the State Government’s statutory account,’” he said. When asked whether the commission could impose a restriction for up to 72 hours before obtaining a court order, Adekilekun rejected that interpretation and insisted that judicial authorisation must come first. “See, in this regard, EFCC must get a court order. The laws are there. If you read the provision I’m talking about, Section 7 of the Money Laundering Act, it stipulates that court order must be served. It is there,” he insisted. He also dismissed allegations that the account was linked to money laundering, stressing that it had only been used to receive allocations from the Federation Account. “You can’t do an act of this magnitude and just say you are transmitting a letter to put a PND on a state government account. The only money that is being transferred to that account is from the Federation Account, pure federal domain. That’s one of the requirements,” he said. His comments came shortly after human rights lawyer and Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Femi Falana, defended the EFCC’s action, saying the commission did not act unlawfully. Falana argued that the EFCC has the authority to freeze a state government account, provided it secures a court order within the legally prescribed period. He referred to a 2022 Court of Appeal decision involving the Benue State Government and the EFCC, which he said confirmed the commission’s power to place a Post No Debit restriction for a maximum of 72 hours before obtaining judicial approval. Amid the dispute, President Bola Tinubu directed the EFCC to return to court to seek the vacation of the order and discontinue the action, citing concerns over the timing of the restriction ahead of the August 15 Osun governorship election. Responding to a question on whether the Osun State Government would continue with its legal challenge despite the President’s intervention, Adekilekun said the next step would be determined by his client. “Well, it depends on what my client thinks, which is the Osun State Government. If they give us the go-ahead, but I think and I believe that it should be tried,” he said.
